## Rejected AOT register-result conventions (2026-10-14)

Neither of these experiments is retained. Both used the validated post-merge
`6b4590ba714a07a4ba361c63640a19a658529858` baseline on macOS arm64. The proposal
was to replace typed method helper output pointers with a two-word return:
full-width scalar or owned boxed payload, plus miss/native/ordinary-result kind.
Admission, Program/access/epoch checks, observable frames and exception handling
were preserved. Original output-pointer helpers remained available.

The first version combined native-only and matched-boxed dispatch with a policy
argument. Its native helper frame grew from 320 to 384 bytes and the result still
spilled during context cleanup. The second separated native-only and matched
helpers and isolated the eager-context output address. Actual assembly then kept
pure results in registers; native frames returned to 320 bytes, and matched
frames used 368 bytes. This removed the intended spill but did not produce a
worthwhile performance improvement.

Each matrix used 11 workloads, a frozen baseline, enabled A/A, and a candidate
compiled with the new convention disabled. Three forks, three warmups and three
300 ms samples at count 4096 yielded 396 measured windows per matrix: all 792
windows are retained, including noisy forks. Runtime aliases had equal length;
loaded libraries and 555 references per configuration were checked before
timing. Values below are whole-workload ns/element, not isolated call latency.
The two enabled medians are shown as a range, not as a confidence interval.

|!Experiment and workload|!Before|!Enabled A/A|!Compile-off|!Change versus before
|Unified: native integer|9.868|10.967-11.017|9.814|11.13-11.64% slower
|Unified: native floating point|11.433|11.901-11.989|11.179|4.09-4.87% slower
|Unified: boxed integer|15.709|15.950-16.103|15.628|1.53-2.51% slower
|Split: native integer|10.023|10.928-11.194|9.923|9.03-11.68% slower
|Split: native floating point|11.401|11.493-11.736|11.763|0.80-2.94% slower
|Split: boxed integer|15.592|15.727-15.808|16.094|0.86-1.38% slower
|Split: boxed floating point|19.512|19.441-19.447|19.239|0.33-0.36% lower; overlapping fork ranges

Native integer fork ranges were separated from baseline and compile-off in both
experiments. Other movements were mixed or overlapped: for example, the split
floating native compile-off control was also slower. The unified experiment's
unrelated floating callback regression did not persist in the split experiment.
Do not credit such movements to a faster method ABI, or infer that register
returns are inherently slower in other implementations.

The split prototype passed 15 selected release test files, 27 cases and 12278
assertions, plus both 555-check IR/AOT reference grids. Coverage included native
and legacy helpers, full-width values, pending exceptions, stack exhaustion,
member effects, debugger attachment and concurrent frame readers. Minimal C++
and LLVM code-generation probes agreed on aggregate returns for arm64/x86-64
Darwin/Linux; x86-64 Windows differed, and Windows targets were excluded. This is cross-target codegen
evidence, not foreign-platform runtime testing. Debug qualification and a new
Java comparison were not pursued after the negative performance result.

The experimental runtime, lowering and test changes were removed. Their patches,
supplemental test source, raw samples, reference outputs, controls and verification
records remain in the [rejected-experiment dataset](results-aot-register-result-rejected-macos-arm64.json).
The existing output-pointer convention remains the baseline. Next work should
target the measured dispatch/admission and member-access costs; another
result-layout variant is not justified by these results alone.

## Rejected AOT receiver-type admission proofs (2026-10-14)

Neither receiver-proof implementation is retained. The frozen baseline was
`fd6aabe6ce1ac5f26efb417853eb9bdc8b655259`; its production sources match the
validated restored runtime from the preceding experiment (the intervening commit
changed documentation/data only). These experiments targeted typed AOT method
dispatch, not a new IR/JIT optimization or Java comparison.

An exact receiver-class match and an admission-time canonical-type proof can
avoid loading the ordinary receiver's type through its class/private-data chain.
The first version stored a boolean in existing PIC-entry padding. The second
folded that proof into an available alignment bit of the existing scalar
comparison word. Neither reconstructed or dereferenced a pointer from that word.
Non-null instantiated types retained their full comparison; unsupported alignment
and missing/disabled proofs retained the original checks. Program, access, epoch,
body, debugger, stack and frame contracts were unchanged.

Each version used a frozen baseline, two identical enabled configurations and a
runtime-disabled proof control. The control was presence-based (including `0`)
and evaluated at admission, not on each call. Eleven workloads, three forks,
three warmups and three 300 ms samples at count 4096 produced 396 measured
windows per version, with independently randomized orders. All 792 windows are
retained. Runtime paths and control environment entries had matching lengths;
loaded libraries and 555 reference outputs per configuration were verified.

Values below are whole-workload ns/element, not isolated call latency. Enabled
ranges show the two A/A medians, not confidence intervals.

|!Version and workload|!Before|!Enabled A/A|!Runtime-off|!Change versus before
|Boolean: native integer|10.080|10.298-10.511|10.258|2.16-4.28% slower
|Boolean: boxed floating point|19.212|19.508-19.521|19.467|1.54-1.61% slower
|Combined key: native integer|10.061|10.072-10.109|10.659|0.11-0.48% slower; effectively flat
|Combined key: native floating point|11.538|11.291-11.431|11.887|0.93-2.14% faster
|Combined key: boxed floating point|19.132|19.681-19.801|19.739|2.87-3.50% slower
|Combined key: effectful integer member|83.899|85.236-85.662|86.036|1.59-2.10% slower

The combined version's boxed-float and effectful-member fork ranges were
separated from baseline. Its native-integer result overlapped baseline; the
small native-float improvement did not justify the other regressions. Other
workloads were mixed or noisy, including one slow effectful-member control fork;
none was dropped. Comparing only enabled versus runtime-off would misleadingly
suggest a useful native-integer improvement: the relevant unchanged baseline
was already as fast as the enabled candidate.

Both versions retained the 240-byte dispatch-entry layout and the native-int
helper's 320-byte stack frame on macOS arm64. The intended dependent type loads
were removed from the proved hit, but the complete native-int helper grew from
477 instructions to 607 (boolean) or 615 (combined key). These code-generation
observations do not establish the exact cause of every timing movement.

The boolean release screen passed 14 test runs, 26 cases and 12704 QUnit
assertions; the combined-key screen passed 13 runs, 25 cases and 12036 assertions.
Both included the C++ receiver/context probes, disabled controls, native/boxed
calls, member effects, frame readers, cleanup/cancellation and both IR/AOT
555-check grids. Initial test-development failures incorrectly expected native
admission for parameterized receivers; the existing exclusion was retained and
the probes corrected before timing. Debug and foreign-platform qualification
were not pursued after the negative measurements.

All experimental runtime and test changes were removed. The restored release
core and 62 matching AOT modules were rebuilt; original method tests passed
3 files, 9 cases and 4905 assertions, plus both IR/AOT reference grids. Source
and runtime-identity checks match the pre-experiment baseline. The
[dataset](results-aot-receiver-proof-rejected-macos-arm64.json) preserves both
patches, raw timings, reference outputs, assembly, restoration and all audit
items. Next work should investigate per-call configuration/initialization guards
and more granular dispatch evidence before another receiver-proof encoding.

## Rejected AOT single-load policy cache (2026-10-14)

The policy-cache prototype is not retained. It replaced four function-static
boolean policy sites in typed method dispatch with a single atomic byte holding
both initialization state and value. A per-object `std::call_once` performed cold
initialization at the original first-use point; acquire/release preserved
publication, independent policies, latching and retry after an exception. No
policy moved to parse time or admission, and existing environment controls kept
their presence-based behavior. Call ABI, lowering, dispatch layout, live guards,
frames and receiver ownership were unchanged.

The frozen baseline was `c6794233ccfc013d74935aeff859ee189092c7ba` on
`feature/performance`. Both matrices compared two identical baseline
configurations with two identical candidate configurations, using randomized
serial execution, equal-length runtime aliases and verified loaded libraries.
All four configurations passed 555 reference outputs before each matrix. Eleven
workloads at count 4096 used three warmups and three measurement samples per
process: the initial matrix had three forks and 300 ms samples (396 windows),
and confirmation had five forks and 400 ms samples (660 windows).

Values below are whole-workload ns/element, not isolated call latency. Each
range contains the two A/A medians, not a confidence interval. Compare before
and after within the same matrix; absolute timings rose between matrices.

|!Matrix and workload|!Before A/A|!Candidate A/A|!Conclusion
|Initial: native integer|9.964-10.014|10.013-10.015|Effectively unchanged
|Initial: native floating point|11.283-11.450|10.908-10.985|2.64-4.73% faster
|Initial: effectful integer member|83.570-84.644|85.856-86.353|1.43-3.33% slower
|Confirmation: native integer|10.343-10.366|10.274-10.475|Mixed; within fork variation
|Confirmation: native floating point|11.760-11.852|11.550-11.645|0.97-2.54% faster
|Confirmation: effectful integer member|87.639-88.207|89.332-89.895|1.28-2.57% slower

Percentage ranges include all combinations of before/after A/A medians. Native
integer calls showed no repeatable benefit. The floating-point gain did not
justify effectful calls getting slower in both matrices. Other workloads were
mixed: an initial integer-callback slowdown did not clearly repeat; confirmation
list mutation medians were higher, with overlapping fork ranges. No noisy sample
was dropped, and these movements do not establish the cause of each regression.

Actual arm64 assembly confirmed the intended removal of one policy load on the
initialized path. Native-only helper frames stayed at 320 bytes, and matched
helpers stayed at 368 bytes. Complete native-int helper sizes fell from 477 to
465 instructions (v1) and from 487 to 475 (v2); floating helpers changed from
444 to 445 and from 460 to 458. These code-generation improvements alone were
not sufficient evidence to retain the candidate.

The candidate passed 14 selected release test runs, 26 cases and 12026 QUnit
assertions, plus both IR/AOT reference grids. Its standalone policy helper also
passed ThreadSanitizer and AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer probes
for concurrent first use, publication, false/true latching, independent objects
and exception retry. This was not a sanitized full-runtime build. New debug,
foreign-platform and Java qualification were not pursued after rejection;
there is no new IR/JIT timing claim.

The first timing driver's terminal output was lost during context compaction.
Its complete 132 child exit records and raw outputs were independently replayed;
the parent exit status remains explicitly unknown. The larger confirmation's
timing and verification exits were directly observed as successful. All 1056
measurement windows, both A/A controls, raw outputs, source changes, assembly,
validation and audit records are preserved in the
[dataset](results-aot-native-policy-rejected-macos-arm64.json).

The original runtime sources were restored, the release core and 62 matching
AOT modules rebuilt, and five original test files passed 14 cases and 6009
assertions plus both reference grids. No policy helper or experimental test
source remains in the production tree.

|!Audit scope|!Pass|!N/A|!Fail
|Retained documentation and research data; all 62 checklist items recorded in the dataset|7|55|0

The audit does not approve the archived prototype for production use.

Next work targets effectful member access. Source tracing shows that the
prehashed update path still resolves declaration/access context before locking
and looking up storage. Exact-class object summaries already cache immutable
member metadata; extending that to polymorphic effectful calls requires a live
receiver/context key and a lifetime/invalidation proof. Keep object locking,
deletion checks, reference/enum/overflow fallbacks and exact-once continuation;
do not cache a raw member pointer across mutations. Another policy-byte encoding
is not justified by these results alone.

## Rejected AOT effectful-member metadata cache (2026-10-14)

The generic context-cache prototype is not retained. It cached positive member
declaration/access decisions and storage-class selection for effectful AOT
updates, avoiding repeated declaration-name comparisons. Four immutable active
entries were keyed by operation slot, live receiver class, defining context and
a new member-metadata generation. Retirement was bounded at 64 allocations per
context; exhaustion or allocation failure used the original update helper.
Native member additions, hierarchy/context changes and class destruction
invalidated metadata. The method-dispatch generation alone was insufficient:
the native `QoreClass::addMember()` API does not advance it.

The cache did not retain a receiver, mutable value or raw member-storage pointer.
The object write lock, deletion check, live storage lookup, inline-integer and
overflow checks, and exact-once continuation all remained. A new internal helper
and AOT lowering passed the context and operation slot explicitly. Compilation
and runtime presence controls allowed the original path; these controls were
tested for correctness, not timed in this experiment.

per process. The initial matrix used three forks and 300 ms samples; confirmation
used five forks and 400 ms samples, with a different randomized order. All 1056

These are whole-workload ns/element, not isolated call latency. Ranges contain
the two A/A medians, not confidence intervals; percentage ranges include all

adverse; native floating calls show no useful repeatable gain. List mutation
changes direction between matrices with wide fork variation. No noisy result
was discarded. These build-level measurements establish the tradeoff, not the
specific cause of movement in unrelated workloads.

## Emitted-code layout calibration and rejected native-entry alignment (2026-10-14)

Baseline `08412d9ea`, runtime unchanged from the restored `b2c7f9143` line.
The calibration completed, but did **not** reproduce the preceding descriptor
prototype's 6-8% callback loss. The follow-up 64-byte alignment candidate also
failed to establish a useful speedup and was removed. These experiments add
900 verified AOT measurement windows, not a retained optimization or Java result.

### Link-only calibration

One frozen compiler/runtime, identical kernel source, and five predeclared
function orders: default, lexicographic, reverse, Random(487), Random(509).
A second default configuration runs the same executable as an A/A control.
Every mapped pre-link section has identical bytes/address/size across the five
objects, including native text and `__QORE,__pcloc`; full object hashes differ
because symbol-table order is not fixed. Normal qcc linking still constructs
the final PC-to-source trailer. Executable path lengths are equal.

Five forks, three warmups and three 400 ms windows per fork, count 4096, seed 7,
randomized order seed 135523: 360 windows. Each cell below spans the six
configuration medians of fork means, in whole-workload ns/element.

|Integer callback|6.881-6.974
|Floating callback|9.045-9.161
|Native integer method|10.469-10.720
|Effectful integer method|88.479-89.828

Selected callback v2/v3 and ordinary/fast caller instructions are identical
after explicit relocation normalization, at different addresses. This modest
variation is not evidence that layout caused the earlier descriptor regression:
that prototype also changed metadata and allocations. The deterministic sample
does not cover every address/cache/branch-placement dimension. No winning layout
was selected, and no hardware-counter causality is claimed.

Four serial diagnostic profiles ran separately from timing on the calibrated

58.20%, with 5.90% in frame unpublication and 5.40% in its entry stack check.

summed inclusive stacks. Sampling identifies locations, not causal latency.
Effectful calls remain spread across local-value handling, dispatch, member
lookup/string comparison and locks. Instrumented durations are not benchmarks.

Candidate release validation passed six files, 13 cases and 3364 assertions,

Next examine an additive register-preserving callee convention at the assembly

## Caller-owned reusable AOT callback frames (2026-10-14)

Baseline `c6dbcc966`. Retain revision D: repeated same-Program integer callbacks
reuse an invocation-owned diagnostic object, while still publishing/unpublishing
it and waiting for concurrent readers on every call. The final matched run
reduces the integer-callback workload from 6.905 to 6.300 ns/element (-8.76%),
or -11.66% against the same rebuilt runtime with reuse disabled. Java measures
1.958 ns/element: Qore remains 3.22x slower. This is not isolated call latency,
Java parity, a general speedup for all calls, or evidence of a performance ceiling.

### Implementation and rejected alternatives

The additive runtime-v4 helpers accept a fixed 208-byte/16-byte-aligned scratch
slot paired with the existing v3 prepared descriptor. Only AOT int()/int(int)
sites in loop regions qualify, with a four-site (832-byte) per-function budget.
The first miss uses v3; a later admitted hit placement-constructs the object,
without heap allocation. A frameless owner-test wrapper tail-calls the hot helper
or v3. The hot helper has an 80-byte C++ frame on this toolchain, versus the old
272-byte unary dispatch frame. Cleanup destroys scratch before releasing its
borrowed cache owner and is idempotent across error cleanup and resumed execution.
The v3 scalar callee ABI and cache layout are unchanged. Existing RuntimeConfig
thread/cache addresses are reused; no new TLS lookup is introduced.

Program identity, live debugger/body admission, readiness, signature/binding,
pending exceptions and physical stack checks remain live. Caller location and
the previous native context refresh each call. The existing frame-reader
publication/removal handshake and materialized-overflow restoration are retained.
Scratch is never shared between threads/invocations. No frame-pointer/unwind
information is removed. The compile-only control is
`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_FUNCREF_FRAME_REUSE=1`; IR/JIT lowering is unchanged.

Before implementing reuse, preserve_most/preserve_all assembly probes were
negative for these callers/toolchain. Changing only the callee expanded cold
spill requirements; matching the cold chain preserved tiny callee bodies, but
actual SCU caller assembly still matched the ordinary convention, including
272/288-byte integer/floating frames. Mismatched probe objects were never linked
or executed. This does not prove those conventions cannot help another caller.

Four reuse revisions were measured with all five predeclared layouts retained:

|!Revision|!Hot integer on/off|!Decision
|A: heap frame inside original helper|+2.27%|Reject; original large helper frame remains
|B: separate hot helper, heap-owned frame|-14.08%|Reject; uncaptured/captured closure controls regress +5.70%/+3.67%
|C: bounded caller scratch, v3 fallback|-8.70%|Revise; uncaptured closure screen still +2.27%
|D: caller scratch plus frameless miss wrapper|-9.51% screening; -11.66% final|Retain with short/control caveats below

A-D each have 540 windows: three forks, three warmups and three 300 ms windows,
count 4096/seed 7; default/sorted/reverse/Random(487)/Random(509) link orders, frozen
baseline/on/off controls, randomized order seed 135571. No winning layout was
selected. B/C/D short screens each add 675 windows using the same verified
binaries: three forks, two warmups, three 200 ms windows, seed 135587; callback
counts 1/17/1024 and closure counts 4096. D summary on/off changes were +0.99%,
+0.73%, -6.89%, +0.80% uncaptured and -0.28% captured. All five D uncaptured
closure layout medians were slightly slower in that screen (+0.11% to +1.97%),
with overlapping fork ranges; the final larger-count closure comparison below
has the opposite sign. Do not claim that every small cost was eliminated.

## Reusable AOT floating callback frames (2026-10-15)

Retain revision B as a targeted improvement, with measured non-target costs.
Against baseline `83a236cf4`, floating callbacks improve from 8.874 to 7.029
ns/element (-20.80%); the same-runtime floating-v3 control is 8.762 (-19.78%).
Fresh matched Java is 2.788, leaving a 2.52x gap. This is not universal
non-regression: closure costs and the identical-executable control below are
part of the retention decision, not discarded outliers.

The additive float()/float(float) runtime-v4 helpers reuse the existing
invocation-owned 208-byte, 16-aligned scratch. Integer and floating loop sites
share the four-slot/832-byte budget. The complete non-throwing callee-v3 proof
permits deferred context; the frame stores no scalar payload, and arguments and
results remain native doubles. Ordinary floating callbacks retain v3 and eager
markers. Both dispatch and callee physical stack checks, live Program/debugger/
body/readiness/binding/pending checks, and per-call publication/removal with
reader completion remain. There is no new heap allocation or TLS access.
Every exit destroys inactive scratch before its borrowed cache owner.

Actual release assembly reduces the floating helper frame from 288 to 80 bytes;
the public wrapper has five instructions and no frame. Assembly was a feasibility
gate, not proof of speed. Only AOT lowering gains this path; IR/JIT are correctness
controls. `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_FUNCREF_FLOAT_FRAME_REUSE=1` selects floating-v3 while
retaining integer-v4; the pre-existing overall frame-reuse control remains.

## Persistent native-method frames rejected (2026-10-15)

Rejected invocation-owned persistent frames for native integer/floating method
calls. The native integer workload improves 2.84% against frozen baseline and
3.16% against the same runtime with reuse disabled, but one of five layouts is
adverse. Native floating and boxed integer calls do not improve in aggregate;
boxed floating gains only 0.84%. Uncaptured closures cost 2.55% versus frozen.
This is insufficient benefit for retaining the new ABI, storage and cleanup.
All runtime/compiler/test changes are removed; the retained integer and floating
callback optimizations are unchanged.

[Complete evidence](results-aot-method-frame-reuse-rejected-macos-arm64.json)
preserves the rejected patch and two new fixtures, all 585 jobs/1755 measured
windows, both compile-only probes, four qualification failures, candidate and
restored-release results, source/artifact identities, raw reference outputs,
the decision and the individual 62-item audit.

### Mechanism, proof and qualification

Unlike the earlier caller-storage experiment, this prototype initialized its
private diagnostic object once and reused it across calls. Each admitted pure
scalar method borrowed the current receiver/PIC only until frame removal and
reader completion, then cleared both target pointers. No target owner or cached
callee context was retained between calls. Both physical stack guards,
full live dispatch/Program/debugger/body/readiness checks and per-call stack
publication/removal remained. Ordinary matched, effect/member and forwarding
paths kept their existing behavior.

Additive method-v3/v4 helpers used a 256-byte aligned slot with a native result
union, avoiding a ninth integer ABI argument. Loop sites shared an 832-byte
budget with existing callback frames; all exits released inactive storage.
Scalar cleanup/reference passes recognized the new helpers. The experimental
compile-off control was `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_METHOD_FRAME_REUSE`.

The first compile-only shape inlined the old diagnostic fallback and retained
320-416-byte helper frames with 869-928 static instructions. A cold noinline
delegate reduced the actual candidate helpers to 112/128 bytes for typed
integer/floating calls and 160 bytes for matched calls, versus 320/368 bytes
for legacy helpers. Static counts were 473/459 and 491/466, versus 477/444 and
487/460 respectively. The caller adds 256 bytes: these are helper sizes, not
total-stack savings or proof of execution gains. Neither probe object was
linked or executed; only the qualified production-shaped prototype was timed.

Candidate release passed 16 files, 35 cases and 13029 assertions, all 64 owned
qmods, and both 555-result IR/AOT grids. Tests covered new scratch budgets,
typed/boxed integer/floating results, receiver replacement/deletion, foreign
Programs/threads, debugger transitions, concurrent stack readers, pending sinks,
forced overflow, context restoration and caught-exception/early-exit cleanup.

Initial failures remain in the evidence: a result-address GEP emitted after a
terminator; two composed boxed-result helper-name regexes; a repeated enum-key
fixture whose second run no longer had a cold cache; and one member-reader
helper-name regex. The GEP insertion was fixed; both ABIs now tested the same
genuine cold-to-warm transition, without weakening its miss/empty-slot checks;
structural assertions accepted old/new helpers. Full selected qualification
then passed. An earlier AST preflight also corrected a hand-written expected
sum from 15 to 14 before candidate compilation or timing.

## Deferred scalar-closure context (2026-10-15)

Retain deferred empty variable markers and parse/call context for admitted AOT
integer closure companions. Five-fork confirmation improves the noncapturing
closure workload 22.04% versus frozen baseline and 23.48% versus same-runtime
eager context; captured closures improve 18.67% against either control. Every
layout improves, with disjoint observed fork ranges. This is a targeted gain,
not universal non-regression: callback controls and one-element invocations
have small adverse aggregates described below. Java parity is not reached.

[Complete evidence](results-aot-closure-deferred-context-macos-arm64.json)
contains all 3765 measurement windows, raw Qore/JMH outputs, source/artifact
identities, reference grids, compile-only and linked assembly, release/debug
qualification, the fixture setup failure and test-only follow-up, and the
individual audit checks. No sample or layout is discarded.

### Mechanism and proof

The existing compiler admits only one bounded straight-line block of at most
64 instructions: one integer parameter/result, no body locals, arbitrary calls,
writes, reference evaluation or generic reentry. Captures are read using an
explicit closure pointer under the existing lock at every source read; repeated
reads are not coalesced. Every companion already calls the full live stack guard
before body work. No compiler, serialized metadata or calling ABI change is needed.

Dispatch retains all live Program, debugger, normal-body identity, PC-map,
signature and pending-error checks plus its physical entry guard. The new
invocation-owned helper publishes the diagnostic frame without installing empty
variable boundaries or swapping parse/call context. A failed callee guard
materializes that state before exception construction; both guards remain.
Frame removal still waits for diagnostic readers. A speculative capture miss
destroys the frame before ordinary execution can resume. No closure owner is
cached or retained, and there is no new heap allocation or caller scratch.
Eager object/class substitution and optional closure-self context are unchanged.
The existing closure AOT frame marker is preserved.

`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_DYNAMIC_CLOSURE_DEFERRED_CONTEXT=1` selects the legacy eager
frame. That diagnostic path is outlined, so its extra call is not treated as
equivalent to the original binary: the separately frozen runtime is essential.
The actual dispatch frame grows from 336 to 352 bytes (306 to 352 static
instructions, plus a 33-instruction cold initialization fragment). Its old
out-of-line eager constructor/destructor work is removed from successful calls;
the numbers are not a total-stack saving or a speed prediction. Integer and
floating callback helpers remain 153 instructions with 80-byte frames, and their
dispatch wrappers remain five instructions. Address/layout identity or a causal
explanation for timing variation is not claimed.

### Qualification and measurement protocol

Frozen source is clean `7744259d4`, using the separately qualified restored
runtime from the preceding rejected-method trial. Candidate release and debug
each pass 21 files, 54 cases, 12260 assertions, all 64 owned qmods and the 555-result
IR and AOT reference grids. The new fixture wraps actual compiled closures and
forces overflow after publication, then verifies error handling, state restoration,
caller locals/captures across stack-block boundaries, successful subsequent calls,
pending sinks, readiness misses, foreign Programs and foreign-thread reattachment.
Existing tests cover mutable/reference/unassigned captures, distinct environments,
wide integers, effects/fallback, debugger attachment, concurrent mutation/readers,
private context, destroyed self and shared-module closure lifetime.

The first fixture setup attempted a one-input batch aggregate, which qcc rejects
before native execution; adding its required second input corrected the fixture.
After timing, review made padded caller execution explicitly AST and gated only
the artificial-limit case on availability of a supported native stack view.
That test-only change passes again in release and debug (one case/18 assertions
each). The measured production sources and both runtime artifacts remain exactly
unchanged. All 64 release qmod aliases are restored; unrelated links are untouched.
Unsupported architectures retain ordinary fixture checks and full production guards.
These are selected tests, not a full-suite, sanitizer, cross-platform or non-SCU claim.

All measurements use macOS arm64, count4096/seed7, three warmups and three 300-ms
windows per fresh process unless noted. Each default/sorted/reverse/shuffle487/
shuffle509 layout uses the exact same executable/object across frozen runtime,
candidate enabled and candidate runtime-off. All loaded library paths and hashes
are checked, with 555 reference outputs per configuration. No task build, test,
profile or evidence analysis overlaps timing. Host frequency/load/thermal state
is not controlled. Values are whole-workload ns/element, not isolated call latency;
Qore aggregates are medians of five layout medians of fork means. Positive changes
are slower. Observed fork ranges are descriptive, not confidence intervals.

## Exact-type closure admission trial rejected (2026-10-15)

The standalone signature-query optimization is not retained. Its proof is valid:
after the existing exact one-parameter `int(int)` checks, the built-in types cannot
need generic substitution. The trial omitted that redundant query in release,
kept a debug assertion and supplied `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_CLOSURE_EXACT_TYPE_PROOF`
as a same-runtime control. Program/debugger/body/map checks, both physical stack
guards, context handling, capture locks and diagnostic publication were unchanged.
No ABI, cache, ownership or compiler-lowering change was involved.

The initial closure gains did not become a convincing overall benefit in the
confirmation: plain/captured closures improved 2.06%/0.81% versus frozen, while
list mutation cost 1.76%. Confirmation variation was wide, including floating
callback fork means around 7-40 ns/element. Every observation is retained; no
outlier removal, causal explanation or statistical-significance claim is made.
Both trial test edits and the runtime edit are restored exactly to the frozen
source baseline. The previous, much larger closure-context improvement remains.

The complete 2955-window record, candidate patch, raw outputs, artifact hashes,
compile-only probe, qualification and full audit are in
`results-aot-closure-admission-rejected-macos-arm64.json`.

grids. Active owned module aliases point to the restored release build. Debug
remains a candidate artifact until the next debug rebuild; it is not the active
release runtime. No full-suite, sanitizer, cross-platform or non-SCU claim.

The linked closure helper retains its 352-byte frame; instruction count changes

## List-mutation attribution and exact scalar coercion (2026-10-15)

The list-mutation regression is reduced, not resolved. A runtime-only guarded
coercion shortcut reduces its feature-branch time by 4.62%, from 245.123 to
233.802 ns/element. Current develop is 210.224 ns in the same session, so the
remaining regression is 11.22%. No Java parity or performance ceiling is claimed.

### Compiler/runtime crossover

The frozen optimized artifacts from the preceding checkpoint were reused:
Apple Clang release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, LLVM 22.1.8 and qcc `-O3`, arm64 macOS.
Develop is `347db1015`; the feature source checkpoint is `d32f73f90` (runtime
unchanged from the preceding checkpoint). Develop's three AOT executables pass
all 555 reference checks unchanged on the feature runtime. Loaded-library
checks confirm the intended runtime, without an identity or ABI override.
This is compatibility evidence for these artifacts, not a general guarantee.

The diagnostic crossover used default/reverse/shuffle-487 layouts, five forks,
three warmups and three measured 300 ms windows, count 4096 and seed 7, with
randomized interleaved blocks (order seed 135941). Each table entry is the median
of three layout medians; each layout median uses five fork means. All 90 jobs /

|!Workload|!Develop executable + develop runtime, ns/element|!Develop executable + feature runtime|!Feature executable + feature runtime
|list_mutate|207.321|168.489|245.164
|list_build|109.753|86.989|89.636

On unchanged develop code, the feature runtime reduces mutation time by 18.73%.
On that same feature runtime, feature-generated mutation code takes 45.51% more
time than develop-generated code. The generated code, rather than a slower
mutation runtime, is therefore the regression target. The list-build control
shows a much smaller generated-code penalty (3.04%).

Assembly inspection finds 390 versus 778 instructions in the complete linked
mutation functions, including cold cleanup. The feature code includes ordinary
scalar-parameter coercion/publication and additional cache/reload work. Generic
lvalue operations conservatively make ordinary parameters runtime-backed because
reference evaluation and destructors can reflect into the frame. The old code's
faster execution is not proof that restoring its visibility assumptions is safe.
Untimed sampling also identifies generic assignment, lvalue handling and
reference cleanup as remaining costs. Instrumented durations are excluded from
the timing datasets; samples do not assign causal latency percentages to helpers.

### Retained first optimization

`qore_rt_coerce_value_aot()` now accepts an already-immediate int/float/bool
unchanged when its live lvalue declaration is the exact canonical built-in type
and no exception is pending. It publishes the same cleanup bits as the ordinary
helper. Wide integers, tag-colliding floats, enums, soft/optional/generic types,
references, nodes and conversions retain the full helper. Runtime assignment,
parameter visibility, reloads, ownership, cancellation and exception paths are
unchanged. `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_EXACT_SCALAR_COERCE=1` disables the shortcut.

This is an AOT runtime change: no compiler/ABI change or new helper symbol.
Already-built, compatible AOT executables benefit. It does not change the
ordinary IR/JIT coercion helper and is not a general IR/JIT speedup claim.

## Exact typed publication: compiler-selected recovery (2026-10-15)

Retained after three iterations: select a dedicated AOT publication helper at
compile time for ordinary canonical `int`, `float`, and `bool` declarations.
The runtime repeats declaration admission, checks immediate input and matching
already-assigned fixed storage, and updates the actual runtime slot. Captures,
references, substituted types, read-only/special declarations, cleared/finalized
or unassigned slots, wide/tag-colliding values, and mismatches retain ordinary
assignment. No reflected value, reload, cancellation check, ownership operation,
or frame is omitted on an unsupported path.

The additive `qore_rt_assign_exact_scalar_local_aot_v1()` and native-EH companion
require newly compiled AOT code and a matching runtime. Existing general helpers,
ordinary IR/JIT, serialized descriptors and RuntimeConfig layout are unchanged.
`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_EXACT_SCALAR_STORE_LOWERING=1` selects old helpers at compilation;
`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_EXACT_SCALAR_STORE=1` disables runtime admission in new artifacts.

### Rejected predecessors and controls

The first runtime-only guard was added to the general helper. It reduced mutation
time by 8.03%, but increased list building by 4.02%, temporary lists by 3.02%, and
the mixed callback pipeline by 2.14%. List-building before/after ranges were
disjoint in all three layouts. It is not retained.

The second version screened immediate values at the general entry and outlined
scalar admission. Assembly confirmed a stack-frame-free non-scalar tail path,
but the entry still imposed type checks on every list publication. Mutation
improved 7.88%; list building regressed 2.15%, closure 3.07%, and pipeline 2.72%.
This version is also not retained. Its release qualification passed; no debug
rerun or commit was made for it.

The retained version moves helper selection to the compiler and appends the new
runtime helpers after existing definitions. The original general helper is again
its seven-instruction tail call, with no scalar guard or configuration lookup.
This is a different mechanism, not a search over favorable code alignments.

## Exact scalar publication witness (2026-10-15)

The additive `qore_rt_assign_exact_scalar_local_aot_v2()` and native-EH companion
return a success flag only after the existing live declaration/storage guard
publishes an immediate scalar without reentry. For ordinary runtime-backed
parameters, the compiler can then reuse the input bits instead of immediately
evaluating the same slot again. Only the direct exception check intervenes.
Every failed guard retains ordinary assignment and reload. Body-local retention,
private/native/fast-entry storage, captures and references are not broadened.

This does not elide tracker rotation, deferred ownership cleanup, cache epoch
publication, consumed-operand cleanup, later invalidation or later reloads.
Signed zero and representable NaN payloads are preserved by the existing
bit-copy float encoding; owning/tag-colliding floats and wide integers fall back.
No slot binding is cached. Existing v1/general helpers, RuntimeConfig layout,
serialized descriptors, old AOT artifacts and ordinary IR/JIT remain unchanged.
New AOT artifacts require matching additive runtime symbols.

`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_EXACT_SCALAR_STORE_RELOAD=1` at runtime retains the exact fast
store but returns zero, forcing the old reload in the identical executable.
At compilation it selects v1 and the ordinary reload. The older store/lowering
disable controls still work and are covered by tests.

## Bounded inline-integer pair allocation removal (optimized AOT)

This checkpoint removes the temporary two-integer list when its dynamic index
is proven to be zero or one and both elements are proven inline integers. It
extends the existing non-escaping, read-only scalarizer; all alias, visibility,
dominance and exception barriers remain. It uses existing integer IR operations,
with no new ABI, runtime helper or calling convention. AOT needs recompilation;
the shared pass also applies to IR/JIT, but only AOT is timed here.

All runtimes are Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`; all executables use `qcc -O3`. Before is
the frozen validated `4cb6acb0a` executable/runtime pair (merged develop
`4f4130fca`). The develop comparison remains frozen optimized `347db1015`, not
the current target tip. `QORE_DISABLE_IR_BOUNDED_PAIR_SCALAR_REPLACEMENT` is used
only while compiling the candidate control. Enabled/control binaries use the
same frozen candidate runtime. The transform changes one internal fast-entry
contract symbol; that name is remapped in the existing reverse/shuffled order
files without moving any entry. Actual function order is verified, and both
temporary-list entry points have zero list-construction calls in candidate
versus one in before/control, for every layout.

Both trials use 4096 items, seed 7, three warmup and three measured 300 ms windows
per fork, three fixed layouts, randomized interleaved configuration blocks and
retained raw output. No owned build/test/profile/analysis runs during timing.
The aggregate is the median of the three layout medians; each fork contributes
its mean of three windows. Values are whole-workload ns/item, not isolated call
latency. Observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

reflective-local synchronization and boxed lifetime checks.

## Fused-local visibility: native loop execution restored (optimized AOT)

The next checkpoint fixes the constant-local cleanup issue identified above.
Fused add-assignment, increment and less-than-branch instructions refer to locals
through metadata. The fixed-aggregate scalarizer now excludes those locals from
its constant-local shortcut, preserving live initializers and preventing changing
indices from being folded to stale constants. Existing native definite-assignment
and context-independence proofs then apply. No runtime helper, opcode, ABI,
reflection/ownership rule or cancellation behavior is changed.

### Canonical AOT trim call setup

After `6f231f67a`, AOT CallDirect specializes the canonical one-argument value
overload of `Qore::trim`. Compilation proves its exact builtin signature, flags,
return type and omitted default. Runtime guards retain ordinary consuming dispatch
for non-string/enum arguments or differing Program/caller contexts. The specialized
frame preserves the canonical parse-option/statement-location transition, flags,
return type, builtin diagnostic frame, class/object context handling and stack
checks. It calls the same Unicode-aware trimming operation on an owned copy.
Argument cleanup, result ownership, exceptions and runtime-local reloads remain
unchanged. Invoke lowering is not specialized.

The fixture exposed an independent pre-existing JIT bug: the name-only fast trim
shortcut stringified a reference instead of trimming its lvalue. Frozen
`ffa3e8019`-source reproduces that failure in JIT; AST, IR and tiered agree on the
correct mutation. The shortcut is removed, preserving ordinary overload resolution.
The legacy byte-oriented helper is not reused. No IR/JIT performance gain is claimed.

## Exact builtin integer list push (2026-10-16)

Retained candidate: specialize an already-proven fresh, assigned, exclusively
owned list's in-place push when both source and element types are exact builtin
`int`. Ordinary optional, unassigned, soft, enum, reference and unproven cases
keep the checked path. Native signed-64-bit and already NaN-boxed values use
separate helpers, so wide integers retain their full range and existing boxes
are shared rather than unboxed and reallocated. This changes LLVM AOT/JIT
lowering, not the ordinary IR interpreter; only AOT performance is measured.

## AOT exact integer list writeback: redundant coercion (2026-10-16)

Retained a compiler-only specialization of the paired store after an exact
integer in-place list push. The originating and destination declarations must
be the same canonical `list<int>` local, non-reference and non-closure, with
both paired local-COW and in-place markers. Only the already-selected exact
integer helper produces this proof. The normal store skips repeated coercion;
**runtime assignment, cache ownership and weak normalization remain**. The
compile-time control is `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_IN_PLACE_INT_LIST_STORE=1`.
This change is AOT-only, not a new interpreter/JIT optimization.

## AOT unchanged integer-list publication (2026-10-16)

The next retained compiler optimization avoids assigning an unchanged list root
back to a runtime-backed AOT body local after an exact in-place integer push.
It requires the preceding same-declaration coercion proof plus a redundant-store
marker, ordinary body-local ownership, no weak assignment or closure use, and
no fast-entry parameter or pre-instantiated entry cleanup owner. The existing
analysis proves adjacent load/push/store operations. The helper cannot replace
the pointer, change the type or invoke user code: the runtime slot already owns
the mutated list. **General COW replacements still publish normally.**

Common cache/reload cleanup, alloca update, cache freshness, exception checks,
cache reference retention/deferred cleanup and consumed-operand cleanup remain.
There is no new helper, runtime ABI, opcode or cancellation change. The compile
control is `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_IN_PLACE_INT_LIST_PUBLICATION=1`. Disabling either
prerequisite integer-push or coercion optimization also prevents admission.
This extension is AOT-only; ordinary IR interpretation and JIT are unchanged.

optimization. Indexed list mutation still uses its generic path.

finds unchanged indirect/closure bodies, object methods/report and callback

disabled changes only list-building/input-building bodies; the mixed changes
are in untimed input preparation. Before's micro entry also differs in one
immediate. Identical hot-body instructions do not exclude layout/cache/allocator
or host effects. Cross-epoch baseline movements are visible and not pooled.

## Borrowed AOT closure miss-route optimization

The candidate based on `4a2960cfa` routes `int(int)` runtime closures directly
to the existing native continuation on a prepared-cache miss. Ordinary
function-reference preparation always rejects this node type before changing
the cache, so that lookup can be bypassed. The live callback stays borrowed:
no closure/capture retention, cache mutation, eager body materialization or
relaxation of Program, debugger, body-identity, readiness, signature, stack,
object/class context or synchronized capture checks. Positive function-reference
hits skip the new type/gate probe; other signatures compile out the change.
No ABI, metadata layout, opcode or cancellation policy changes.

`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_CLOSURE_MISS_ROUTE=1` is a runtime control. It uses the exact
candidate executable and library, not a relink. The disabled control still
contains the new branch and compiler inlining/layout decisions, so its result
must not replace comparison with the unchanged baseline.

### Optimized measurement

Both runtimes are Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, LLVM 22.1.8, with `qcc -O3`
executables. Eighteen micro/four mixed workloads use default, reverse and
shuffle-487 function order. The three-fork screen and independent five-fork
confirmation use randomized interleaving (seeds 136247/136253), three warmup
and three measured 300ms windows, 4096 items/seed 7. All 1782 + 2970 = 4752
windows remain, including outliers; no retries or pooling. Confirmation reuses
the frozen artifacts. Values are whole-workload ns/item, not isolated call
latencies. No owned build/test/profile/analysis overlaps timing.

The predeclared rule requires both closure workloads to improve at least 2%
against both controls in both epochs, with improvement in every layout. A
non-target kernel/layout/control pair with a disjoint adverse fork-mean range
and at least 3% median slowdown in both epochs rejects the candidate. This
candidate passes. This rule is a retention decision, not statistical proof of
universal non-regression.

### Retention decision and adverse results

The rule required both closure workloads to improve at least 2% in aggregate
against both controls in each trial, with improvement in every layout, and no
repeated non-target kernel/layout/control slowdown of at least 3% with disjoint
fork-mean ranges. Both closure targets passed: all twelve target comparisons
have disjoint faster ranges in the screen, and ten of twelve in confirmation;
all target layout medians improve. The following repeated adverse pairs fail
the regression criterion. No third rescue trial or alignment search was run.

### Code review, correctness, and next checkpoint

The compiler already requires canonical builtin `int(int)` without type
substitution before emitting the dynamic closure companion. Fresh signature
reconstruction resolves builtin `int` canonically before variant publication;
the existing release/acquire binding and live normal-body identity match the
proof to its owner. The rejected candidate kept same-Program, debugger,
readiness, physical-stack, pending-exception, lexical-context and synchronized
capture checks. The source proof remains an architectural observation, not a
retained runtime shortcut.

Relocatable instruction comparison preserves all immediates and rebases only
local branch destinations: 149 of 150 micro functions and all 29 mixed functions
match. The sole micro difference is `_main`'s metadata-length argument
(`0x7ba2` before, `0x7b9d` candidate); no timed loop body changes. Runtime
disassembly confirms the default signature-check bypass and its rechecked
control. Untimed captured-closure samples still show native admission/context
handling and synchronized capture loads. These observations do not establish
the cause of the list-building regression or override it. Host load, frequency,
thermals, allocation placement and code/cache layout remain uncontrolled;
observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

New `AOTClosureSignatureProof.qtest` covers exact/captured integer companions,
wide signed boundaries and ten ineligible optional/soft/auto/enum/float/arity
shapes. It checks AST/IR/JIT/tiered and stripped AOT O0/O3, EH, no-debug,
split-compilation and native-disabled behavior, plus compiler selection. Its
208 assertions passed on the unchanged baseline before editing production code.
Candidate and freshly restored Release/Debug qualifications each pass 57 files,
89 cases and 10799 assertions, plus HTTP 10 cases/30 assertions, offline LLM
4/23, cancellation 22/110 and 555 references per IR/AOT. Debug native tests pass
1082 tests in each bounded-pair state; abrupt-drop passes four assertions
in Debug and skips Release. Each Debug wrapper restores exactly 64 owned Release
module aliases. This is selected macOS arm64 qualification, not full-suite,
sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

The next checkpoint refreshes matched optimized branch/develop/Java timings,
including every call family and mixed Qore workloads. Follow-up optimization
must use a distinct evidence-backed hypothesis; this unchanged implementation
will not be retried to search for a favorable layout. Java parity and a global
performance ceiling remain unestablished.

Full samples, artifact hashes, candidate patch, source-proof review, both trials,
all qualification logs, exact rollback, disassembly, profiles and the complete
audit-changes checklist are in
`results-aot-closure-signature-proof-rejected-macos-arm64.json`.

## Rejected guarded integer-list COW append (2026-10-17, post-4428adbb2)

**No production optimization is retained.** AOT list mutation still uses the
ordinary append/coercion/publication path. The candidate specialized an adjacent
runtime-backed local append with a declared canonical `list<int>` and an exact,
assigned integer value. Its corrected helper checked the actual live list's
validity and integer element metadata, preserved natural-reference-count COW,
owned results, wide-box identity and sparse slots, and kept ordinary paired-store
coercion, local cleanup/reload and replacement publication. Other inputs used the
unchanged generic helper. No new serialized opcode or layout was introduced.

An initial declaration-only proof also skipped paired-store coercion. It passed
Release value checks but failed a Debug assertion when reflection replaced the
local with a plain list. A declaration is not proof of current runtime metadata.
That proof/map was removed before any timing. The strengthened test checks AOT
metadata inside the function, before return filtering can hide a missing store
coercion. Frozen baseline AOT O0/O3 passes this check; AST intentionally retains
plain-list metadata there, so that additional assertion is explicitly AOT-only.
Ordinary value output still matches AST/IR/JIT/tiered. The initial failed Debug
build, successful-but-insufficient Release checks and both binaries are archived.
Two diagnostic fixture mistakes (a C++-style comment in Qore and an overly broad
AST metadata expectation) were corrected against baseline before qualification.

## Object-removal baseline correction before inline lvalue records

Expanded baseline testing found an existing Debug assertion in the AOT
`DgcRemoveScanChecks` module before any inline-record implementation or timing.
Removing a child's last object-valued member incorrectly decremented the
parent's scan count although the parent still held the child. Empty objects
remain scan-relevant values. A minimal repeated-removal case reproduced this
in AST, IR, JIT, tiered mode and AOT, for both single members and slices.

The correction removes those two false parent-delta updates. Child member
accounting, access checks, locks, removed-value lifetime and recursive-set
scans remain intact. Regression cases repeatedly remove through object,
hash and list parents and the Debug reference API, then create a back edge
and check exact destruction counts. Additional strong/weak/opaque edge probes
preserve live objects and release them exactly once; four AOT cases abort in
the original frozen runtime and all 30 cases complete after the correction.
These cases are also added to the permanent fixture before final qualification.
Compiled-module tests cover O0/O2/O3;
source tests include tiered mode. Native record-order/clear/move/borrowed-owner
tests add 789 assertions without changing the vector representation.

Fresh Release and Debug each pass 59 core fixtures /
92 cases / 11621 assertions. Additional
lvalue/DGC qualification passes 13 fixtures /
82 cases / 1330 assertions
in Release and 13 / 82 /
2663 in Debug, plus HTTP, offline LLM, thread and
cancellation checks and 555 IR + 555 AOT references. Debug native tests pass
1871 assertions in each bounded-pair mode. Exactly 64 Release module aliases
are restored. This is selected macOS arm64 qualification, not full-suite or

## Fully deferred scalar closure context v2 (2026-10-17, post-a0e895a56)

Retained after both predeclared epochs pass. Optimized confirmation reduces
plain closure workload time from **19.735 to 18.021 ns/item (-8.682%)**, and
captured closure time from **25.825 to 24.815 ns/item (-3.911%)**. Both improve
in all three fixed layouts in both epochs. These are whole-workload costs,
not isolated call latencies or a fresh Java/develop comparison.

There is a material caveat: effectful boxed-method time increases **2.316% in
screen and 2.918% in confirmation**; all layouts are slower in both epochs.
Confirmation/default is **5.021% slower with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges**.
Shuffle has smaller disjoint losses in both epochs. This is not a universal
non-regression result, even though the predeclared repeated >=3% rule passes.
No loss is discarded on the basis of unchanged generated instructions.

### Contract and method

An append-only atomic v2 binding publishes the existing scalar closure companion
after the bounded IR proof and a complete lowered-function call proof. V1 retains
its eager object/class/self context. V2 constructs the same immutable per-call
diagnostic frame but defers object/class/self lookup and substitution until a
guard materializes context for exception handling. It keeps all identity, ready
PC-map, same-Program, debugger, signature, pending-sink and physical stack checks.
The frame is unpublished and readers are waited for before borrowed metadata dies.
Materialization is caller-first; live and compatibility-snapshot views are saved
independently and restored through the current RuntimeConfig implementation.
No extra closure ownership, capture caching, read coalescing or lock removal.

The <=1024-instruction lowered proof allows only lifetime hints, one entry-block
live stack guard with matching arguments, and synchronized capture-read helpers.
Unknown or indirect calls fail closed. Cancellation is checked every 100 instructions
and propagates as compilation failure. No serialized stride or existing field
offset changes; compiled artifacts require the new binder and matching runtime.

Qualified Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, qcc `-O3`, LLVM 22.1.8; 4096 items / seed 7,
three warmup and three measured 300 ms windows. Default/reverse/shuffle-487 layouts,
18 micro/four mixed workloads. Three-fork screen/order 136337 and independent
five-fork confirmation/order 136343 use exactly the same frozen executables,
without relinking. Both targets must improve >=2% in aggregate and improve every
layout in both epochs. Reject a repeated non-target >=3% adverse layout median
with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges in both epochs. All 3168 windows retained;
no pooling, rescue epoch, best-layout selection or alignment search. Ranges are
not confidence intervals. Every artifact passes 555 micro / 60 mixed reference checks
and its actual loaded-library check.

### Rejected implementation and diagnosis

The candidate added a seven-argument v3 entry after a complete bounded v2 proof,
cloning the scalar body and replacing only its full stack helper with a live-bound
load and physical-SP comparison. Null/unsupported/exhausted views tail to the
original full-guard body before scalar work. Existing v1/v2 entries, dispatcher
physical-stack check, same-Program/identity/debugger/signature/sink guards,
synchronized capture reads, immutable diagnostic frames, reader waits and context
restoration remain. No new owner, capture coalescing or cached limit value.
Equality is checked structurally by the unsigned LLVM predicate, not by injecting
the exact generated SP at runtime. New context slot and generated code increase
size; compile-time, footprint and cold-start performance were not measured.

Generated-code review covers 179 common functions plus three new v3 companions.
Original dynamic companions are unchanged; three normal closure entries add five
instructions each for binding, and both main functions change initialization
metadata. Other common instructions are unchanged after local-branch rebasing.
The plain new body has a transient 16-byte frame; captured companions use 48 bytes
versus 64 in the original full-guard bodies. Captured reads remain synchronized.
The runtime forms the live limit address inline, but still performs dispatcher
admission, a 352-byte dispatcher frame, frame publication and indirect dispatch.
Nine runtime disassemblies and four serial untimed samples are preserved. Profiles
show v3 selection and remaining type/node/signature/frame/capture-lock work; they
cannot attribute broad losses or establish an isolated cost. Signal-wait samples
are helper-thread waiting, not active closure cost. No profile duration is timed data.

### Implementation and diagnosis

The rejected change follows only QoreValue Phi ancestry in an independent
visited-on-enqueue worklist, with cancellation every 100 combined seeds/nodes/edges,
to extend an existing profitability hint for ordinary read-only auto parameters.
It does not change the direct-receiver set used by weak-load cleanup. All existing
stored-local/reference/capture/weak/opaque/private-entry exclusions and runtime
strong-slot/identity/epoch/entry-owner/reload guards remain. No ABI/runtime helper change.

Before candidate build or timing, source inspection established that generic
lvalue member writes classify their roots as stored. The original effectful target
therefore remains excluded. The original plan and its pre-build amendment are both
preserved: object_loop is the target; effectful methods remain a control. Its
observed gains cannot be attributed to the new cache. No write/COW/reference guard
was weakened to force a benefit.

Generated-code review compares all **196 common functions** (150 micro / 29 mixed /
17 probe), with no added/removed functions. Seven ordinary micro receiver bodies,
two ordinary probe bodies and three main initialization immediates change. Private
native entries remain unchanged. The ordinary boxed-int method grows from
1421 to 1512 instructions and **432 to 512 bytes of stack**; each ordinary probe
body grows from 1534 to 1666 instructions and **768 to 848 bytes of stack**.
Three admission calls and per-read epoch guards add work even where another fast
continuation is already efficient. This is an observed mechanism, not a measured
causal decomposition of the regression. Static reload sites are not dynamic counts.

Eight runtime helper disassemblies preserve strong-slot selection, saturating
pre-assignment invalidation and owner-safe stale reloads. Four serial untimed
profiles show the object probe still using generic method dispatch, diagnostic
frame/string work, context transitions, member-name lookup and synchronized getter
loads. Strings continue through pseudo-method dispatch/conversion. Parent/child
samples are not summed, and signal-wait samples are idle helper-thread work.
Profiles are excluded from timing. Unchanged generated bodies do not justify
discarding adverse results.

### Contract and review

Separate append-only integer/float zero-argument companions take borrowed receiver,
defining class, same-thread RuntimeConfig, accepted output, exact AOT context and
sink. The existing unary ABI, compact Program/type witness and effect-prefix
contract are unchanged. A one-block / at-most-64-instruction whole-body proof requires
exactly one member read and a strict scalar return family; calls, branches, effects,
locals/ARGV/explicit-self/opaque access and unsupported signatures stay ordinary.

Existing full-key name/pre-resolved PIC lookup retains receiver/type/access/parse-
options/epoch/Program checks. Separate immutable signature admission never caches
negative lazy publication. Exact normal-body binding, live readiness/body/receiver/
Program/debugger/stack guards and synchronized member loads remain. No value or lock
is cached. Eager explicit object/class context and the existing logical native frame
are retained. The borrowed PIC name is unpublished and reader-safe before a miss can
enter generic code and replace its owner. Results preserve ordinary boxing/ownership.

Generated-code review covers all 199 common functions plus 2 new getter
companions; fixed non-default layouts place each companion immediately after its
normal body, without alignment search. 13 runtime disassemblies
cover ordinary dispatch, separate getter dispatch/publication and synchronized reads.
Six serial untimed samples cover before/candidate integer, float and string loops.
Static instruction counts are not dynamic call counts; profile samples are not
isolated latencies, and unchanged bodies do not justify discarding adverse timings.
Detailed manually reviewed findings are preserved in the JSON evidence.

### Contract and diagnostics

The shared method PIC layout and existing ordinary/unary dispatch source remain
unchanged. Separate typed six-pointer zero-argument getter companions use the bounded
one-block/64-instruction/exactly-one-member-read proof and synchronized live reads.
Full receiver/type/access/Program/parse-options/epoch and applicable parse-selected
identity checks precede invocation. Exact normal-body binding, readiness, signature,
debugger and stack checks remain. RuntimeConfig is passed from the caller; no member
value is cached, no lock is elided and no unary witness is reinterpreted.

After a complete matching cache key, ordinary continuation first attempts existing
fast dispatch. A non-fast-eligible name-resolved call directly evaluates the matched
variant with the checked context; exact parse-selected calls use the existing
method dispatcher. This avoids restarting name lookup on that matched path. Method
and variant pointers are copied before arbitrary execution, with no later PIC access.
Native getter invocation is separately outlined; eager object/class substitution
and reader-safe logical-frame teardown finish before any ordinary continuation.
Unmatched, foreign-Program, static and parameterized routes retain existing fallback.

Generated-code review covers 207 common functions plus 2 getter companions.
Runtime review covers 23 disassemblies, including float-unary calls,
local assignment, complete getter dispatch, outlined invocation and synchronized
reads. Fourteen serial untimed profiles cover before/candidate getter, default,
string-result, two-read, boxed-float and monomorphic workloads. Static instruction
counts and sample counts are not dynamic call costs or causal allocations of time.

All 5,904 measured windows are retained: 738 screen jobs / 2,214 windows and 1,230 confirmation jobs / 3,690 windows. Both target aggregate/all-layout checks pass. Five repeated adverse non-target/layout pairs fail the unchanged gate: boxed-float/default and reverse, monomorphic/default, and string-result/reverse and shuffle. No rescue epoch, pooling, retuning or layout search.

Confirmed whole-workload ns/item: integer getter 281.552562 -> 131.036341 (-53.459%); floating getter 313.602194 -> 137.776774 (-56.066%); default loop 700.657242 -> 709.627780 (+1.280%); boxed float 19.697728 -> 20.662681 (+4.899%); string result 407.519869 -> 447.565386 (+9.827%). Effect loop +6.835% and two-read loop +6.464% also remain visible, even though their observed ranges do not trigger the repeated-disjoint gate. Monomorphic aggregate -1.228% does not erase its default-layout +6.565% loss.

Generated comparison covers 150 micro, 29 mixed and 28 probe common functions, plus two new companions. Micro changes integerArg (normal/fast) and the main compressed-metadata size; mixed changes integerArg (normal/fast) and orderReport; probe changes binders, integerArg (normal/fast), main and three loop callers. Boxed-float and monomorphic hot caller bodies are unchanged. Compared with the previous isolated candidate, only micro/probe main compressed-metadata-size constants differ across 209 generated functions.

Runtime review covers 23 disassemblies. Ordinary name dispatch has 2,202 static instructions, fast dispatch 2,411, ordinary dot dispatch 153 with a 0x70 frame, and local assignment 137 in both runtimes. The four synchronized read helpers have 47/45/45/44 instructions in both. Float-unary changes from 460 to 468 instructions, with the same 0x170 frame and call multiset but different guard/cold-block code. Getter public dispatch has 435 instructions / 0x100 frame; outlined invocation 562 / 0x190; complete ordinary continuation 70 / 0x40; binders 33 each. Static counts are not dynamic costs, and address-sensitive linked code is not claimed identical.

Fourteen serial untimed samples cover before/candidate getters, defaults, string results, two-read, boxed-float and monomorphic calls. Getter invocation/frame setup and dispatch guards remain prominent, alongside local loads, reference counting and member lookup. The default profile directly reaches NormalMethodFunction::evalMethodTmpArgs from the matched ordinary continuation, avoiding the earlier redundant name-dispatch restart. String-result/two-read profiles still pass through the speculative getter wrapper before ordinary fast execution. Samples do not partition the measured regression causally.

Boxed-float samples are dominated by qore_rt_try_method_float_unary_v2, the unchanged generated caller and local assignment; the zero-argument getter helper is not its hot route. Its runtime helper changed despite unchanged source. Monomorphic samples remain dominated by the unchanged generated body. Placement, cache and compiler-global effects remain hypotheses; none justifies discarding a repeatable loss.

An untimed compiled size probe reports QoreAOTContext at 880 -> 896 bytes, alignment 8; both sizes map to 896 bytes via malloc_good_size. The shared PIC entry remains 240 bytes, alignment 8. There is no allocator-bucket increase for this type on this host. Metadata compaction is not selected merely on a speculative bucket explanation; no runtime allocation trace or general cache conclusion is claimed.

Candidate Release and Debug each pass 69 core files / 112 cases / 17,595 assertions, including four getter cases / 1,053 assertions. The 13 lvalue/DGC suites, HTTP/offline LLM/thread integrations, 555 IR plus 555 AOT references, 1,985 Debug native checks per bounded-pair mode, and restoration of 64 module aliases pass. This is not full-suite, sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

Next investigate positive compiler-published getter admission within an already-matched ordinary route, avoiding blanket rewriting of zero-argument callers and unsupported-call overhead. Separately assess compile-time exclusion of provably non-object receivers and native context/proof deferral. Preserve full live guards, exact publication and ownership. These are unmeasured hypotheses, not already validated fixes.

This is an AOT-only experiment, with no fresh Java/develop ratio. Probes include two receiver calls, a callback and setup; short variants also include ordinary call_function. Future Java getter comparisons must make synchronization explicit. Java parity and a global performance maximum remain open.

and actual terminal statuses remain recorded; no failed or incomplete run is
represented as qualification. Selected macOS arm64 validation, not full-suite,
sanitizer or cross-platform certification. No compile-time, memory-footprint,
cold-start, cross-Program or application-wide performance claim.

Next test positive compiler-published getter admission within already-matched

and a justified global performance ceiling remain open.

### Contract and review

Separate append-only integer/float zero-argument companions take borrowed receiver,
defining class, same-thread RuntimeConfig, accepted output, exact AOT context and
sink. The existing unary ABI, compact Program/type witness and effect-prefix
contract are unchanged. A one-block / at-most-64-instruction whole-body proof requires
exactly one member read and a strict scalar return family; calls, branches, effects,
locals/ARGV/explicit-self/opaque access and unsupported signatures stay ordinary.

Caller-selected zero-argument dispatch leaves the shared PIC layout and existing
name/pre-resolved/unary dispatch source unchanged. RuntimeConfig is acquired/reused
once in the logical caller entry. Full receiver/type/access/parse-options/epoch/
Program and applicable parse-selected identity checks remain; no negative lazy
publication is cached. Exact normal-body binding, live readiness/body/receiver/
Program/debugger/stack guards and synchronized member loads remain. No value or lock
is cached. Eager explicit object/class context and the existing logical native frame
are retained. The borrowed PIC name is unpublished and reader-safe before a miss can
enter generic code and replace its owner. Results preserve ordinary boxing/ownership.

Generated-code review covers all 207 common functions plus 2 new getter
companions; fixed non-default layouts place each companion immediately after its
normal body, without alignment search. 18 runtime disassemblies
cover ordinary dispatch, separate getter dispatch/publication and synchronized reads.
Fourteen serial untimed samples cover before/candidate integer/float getters, defaults,
string results, two-member reads, boxed-float methods and monomorphic calls.
Static instruction counts are not dynamic call counts; profile samples are not
isolated latencies, and unchanged bodies do not justify discarding adverse timings.
Detailed manually reviewed findings are preserved in the JSON evidence.

The candidate's ordinary continuation attempts existing fast dispatch after a full
cache-key match, but a non-fast-eligible method then falls back to full dot/name
lookup again. Source and default-loop samples confirm this redundant path for default
arguments. The new public helper has 813 static instructions and a 0x1e0 stack frame;
ordinary dot dispatch has 153 instructions and a 0x70 frame in both runtimes. This
motivates an outlined getter invocation and complete already-resolved ordinary fallback,
not a quantified attribution of the regression. Boxed-float/monomorphic caller bodies
are unchanged, yet their repeated adverse layouts remain grounds for rejection;
placement/cache effects are hypotheses, not established explanations.

### Contract and diagnostics

Five original first-use controls retain distinct template/call-site scope, exact getenv expressions, short-circuit order and presence semantics. A constinit typed atomic state supplies the hot result; outlined initialization retains the original C++ local-static guard, exception retry and immutable result. No caller/compiler/PIC/AOT-context layout, dispatch-key, live-body, Program, debugger, stack, context, ownership or locking change. Acquire/release publication preserves initializer visibility; racing first callers publish only the same successful value.

Each call-site/template instance keeps independent first-use initialization.
The original local-static initialization guard and immutable result remain on the
cold path. A separate typed atomic state is published with release/acquire ordering.
No environment value is observed earlier at binding or compilation, and empty or
`"0"` disabling values still count as present. The added static state and outlined
code are not free; linked file/section sizes are recorded separately, not presented
as heap-allocation or cache measurements.

Generated-code review covers 207 common functions and 0 new functions.
Post-timing runtime review covers 24 disassemblies; pre-timing
inspection also records all four unary entry versions and sixteen separate cold
initializers. Fourteen serial untimed samples cover integer/floating boxed calls,
their ordinary fallbacks, effectful integer calls, closures and monomorphic calls.
Instruction and sample counts are not dynamic costs or causal allocations of time.

The fixed three-fork screen rejects the candidate: boxed integer16.222507922550->16.747640414271ns/item (+3.237061% time), boxed float19.962669002259->20.946258325133ns/item (+4.927143%). Both targets worsen in all three layouts instead of meeting the required2% aggregate gain/every-layout improvement. All2214windows remain; no confirmation or rescue run was performed.

Target per-layout changes are integer default+3.374750%, reverse+3.282127%, shuffle+2.861266%; float default+6.475373%, reverse+4.653862%, shuffle+6.110584%. The three integer observed fork ranges overlap; all three float ranges are disjoint adverse. These observed ranges are not confidence intervals. The fixed target gate fails regardless; this is not a statistically certified universal slowdown.

Non-target disjoint adverse screen pairs at least3% include temporary_hash/default+4.861451%, boxed_float_method_fallback/default+4.765893% and reverse+3.305578%. No repeated adverse pair can be claimed from a single epoch. Every smaller loss and apparent gain is also retained in the41-workload table, not pooled into a success claim.

All207 common generated functions (150micro,29mixed,28probe) have identical normalized relocatable instructions; none is added or removed. Caller/compiler source and PIC/AOT-context layout are unchanged. Runtime review records24disassemblies. Ordinary name/fast/dot dispatch, auto-local assignment and four member-read helpers retain their instruction counts and call-target multisets; that is not a claim of identical addresses or timing.

Unary runtime entry instruction counts change intv1477->464, intv2487->474, floatv1444->445 and floatv2460->458, with no padding in those four entry disassemblies. v1 frames remain0x140 and v2 frames0x170. Direct-plus-indirect call-site counts remain21/22/19/20 respectively. Cold-initializer disassemblies can contain trailing udf padding, so earlier approximate row counts there are not executable work. None of these static counts gives dynamic cycles.

RCpc-aware supplementary inspection confirms a single acquire state load per visited control, distinct initialization guards and release publication for16 cold cache instances; both matched-fallback lambdas also use the same state path. Enabled expression bodies may be compiler-merged without merging cache state or first-use scope. The new enabled path branches over a cold block where the old guard/value path fell through. Branch/code placement is a possible investigation, not an established cause or permission for layout/padding search; the tested candidate is rejected unchanged.

All14 serial untimed samples finish successfully. Boxed targets sample the unary helpers, generated loops, stack checks/publication and auto-local result assignment; float also samples result conversion. No QoreNativeControlCache initializer appears in these sampled stacks. Absence from samples does not prove zero cold cost. Fallback-labelled workloads currently sample admitted synchronized scalar-member paths, including live member lookup/hash comparison and read-lock operations; they must not be described as exclusively ordinary dispatch. Effectful calls retain local/reference/locking work. Closure and monomorphic controls keep their established routes. Profiles are diagnostics, not benchmark windows or isolated-cost estimates.
