### Contract and diagnostics

Append-only six-pointer zero-argument strict int/float getter companions with unchanged shared PIC layout and generated caller selection. Reuse a full-key-matched generic admission inside existing ordinary fast dispatch; only a positive exact-body getter binding enters the outlined native helper. Generic admission alone is not native authorization. Preserve current body/readiness/Program/debugger/stack/signature guards, eager object/defining-class context, synchronized live member reads, boxing and reader-safe frame teardown before existing ordinary fallback. RuntimeConfig is acquired only after positive admission and passed explicitly within the invocation; this route still has TLS acquisition. No public speculative caller helper, second PIC scan, negative binding cache, unary-witness widening, member-value caching or lock elision.

The implementation is limited to four runtime/compiler files and three fixtures.
The shared PIC and generated caller selection are unchanged. Unsupported or
unpublished getters avoid the outlined native frame; absent bindings are not cached
negatively because ordinary execution can publish them later. Default-argument
methods do not meet the zero-declared-parameter admission. Static, copy,
parameterized, debugger and cross-Program routes retain their existing behavior.

Generated-code review covers 207 common functions and 2 new companions;
normal getter bodies need binder calls, so identical source selection is not a
claim that all machine instructions remain identical. Runtime review records
21 disassemblies. Fourteen serial untimed profiles cover
getter targets and default, string-result, two-read, boxed-float and monomorphic
controls. Footprint observations are separate from timing. Static instruction and
sample counts are not isolated costs or causal allocations of time.

All 207 common default-layout relocatable functions were compared, with local branch destinations rebased and constants/registers/external symbols retained. Exactly 203 are normalized-instruction-identical. The micro main has one changed immediate; the probe main has one changed immediate. The two ordinary getter bodies add their exact-body binder and corresponding register/branch changes. All 29 mixed functions and the probe workload callers remain identical under this comparison. Only two functions are added: independent integer and float getter companions; no function is removed. Static identity does not establish identical placement or timing, and no adverse timing was excluded on this basis.

Both new companions receive six pointers with a typed scalar return. Actual optimized assembly retains the explicit RuntimeConfig stack guard, exactly one prehashed live scalar-member-read helper, and accepted=0 on a representation miss. There is no generic self-member load or speculative public caller helper in either companion. The ordinary getter remains available for fallback, including conversion and ownership handling.

The 21 runtime disassemblies include both versions of name dispatch, ordinary fast dispatch, dot dispatch, float unary dispatch, auto-local assignment, and four scalar-read helpers, plus the new invocation and two binders. Positive-binding acquire loads occur only after ordinary admission. The invocation retains exact body/readiness, zero-arity and strict-return checks, obtains RuntimeConfig after admission, installs actual defining-class/object context and a reader-safe logical frame, and tears that state down before effect-free fallback. Large integer boxing, floating representation, sink ownership, QoreJITException handling and stack guards remain. The binders use first-valid release CAS; the raw LSE opcode in the disassembly is not treated as a missing instruction. The ordinary dot/unary/local/read routes retain their corresponding helper calls; this is not a claim that all runtime machine code is identical.

Fourteen untimed before/candidate profiles completed successfully. The candidate integer and float probe profiles enter the admitted getter helper. Default-argument profiles still show default preparation/allocation, string-result profiles retain generic dispatch and string conversion, and two-read profiles retain generic member lookup. Boxed-float profiles remain dominated by the existing unary helper/caller and local assignment; monomorphic profiles remain dominated by the generated workload loop. Sampling is diagnostic only: these counts are not isolated call costs, causal cycle savings, or additional benchmark measurements.

The size probe measured QoreAOTContext 880 to 896 bytes, with both requests in the current macOS 896-byte malloc_good_size bucket. The shared PIC entry remains 240 bytes with alignment 8. This establishes neither zero memory cost nor a cache-effect explanation for any timing change.

The independent 5-fork confirmation measured integer getter workload 284.2049278366459 to 168.7309940244433 ns/item (-40.630518%), float 330.2612373687563 to 175.2148939673726 (-46.946576%), integer short 1200.88766828618 to 1066.3755849939614 (-11.201055%), and float short 1260.2385434169832 to 1094.197198177312 (-13.175390%). The two loop targets are faster in every layout in both epochs. These workloads include two receiver calls, a callback and setup/loop costs; they are not single-call latencies.

All 5904 measured windows and smaller or single-epoch losses are retained. There is no repeated same-workload/same-layout adverse result meeting the frozen 3% plus disjoint observed fork-mean-range gate. Single-epoch qualifying losses remain: screen indirect/default +4.504364%, screen callback-pipeline/default +3.218793%, and confirmation indirect-wide/default +3.154075%. Confirmation string-result aggregate is +3.181453%, versus screen -0.186883%; this is not erased or described as zero regression. Observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

Actual source review found no required change to the frozen candidate: bounded compile-time proof, eager receiver/class context, exact normal-body publication, unchanged unary contract, existing live synchronized representation/deletion checks, and reader-safe teardown are retained. Release and Debug qualification and control/reference runs passed at the recorded source identities. The final automated 62-item audit is still a separate required step before commit.

This is an AOT-only new companion path. RuntimeConfig is passed explicitly inside the accepted invocation, but its acquisition and the ordinary dispatch TLS reads remain. No fresh Java/develop ratio or global performance ceiling is claimed. Next: a matched optimized feature/develop/Java checkpoint, followed by a separately measured experiment threading the already-acquired live RuntimeConfig through ordinary dispatch, preserving cross-Program and fallback behavior.

read twice with an identity callback between reads, and accumulate integer results.

callback inlining. Read-lock controls additionally use a standard nonfair Java
read/write lock per receiver; this is not Qore's member lock or an equivalent
implementation of Qore dynamic lookup/deletion, context, frames and cancellation.

### Qualification, diagnostics and next work

Fresh merged Release and Debug each pass 69 core files / 112 cases / 17595
assertions, including the getter's 1053 assertions, plus lvalue/DGC, HTTP,
offline LLM, thread, native/reference and merged DataProvider coverage. All
64 owned qmods are rebuilt and their Release aliases restored; unrelated links
are unchanged. Each comparison executable passes its micro555/mixed60/probe168
reference grid; Java passes 555 existing and 72 getter checks. Loaded-library
identity, optimized build settings and every fixed symbol order are verified.
The report contains exact per-suite counts and full child exit/log provenance.
This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer certification.

Fast same-Program workloads are substantially improved over develop, but not at Java parity. Direct and method work are 1.537 and 1.602 ns/item versus Java 0.935 and 0.974 (both about 1.64x Java time); monomorphic 3.493 versus 1.685 (2.07x), indirect 6.732 versus 1.716 (3.92x), polymorphic 22.307 versus 2.529 (8.82x), and capturing closure 23.925 versus 1.767 (13.54x). These include their loop work, and the documented Java dynamic/callback no-inline controls remain in place.

The dynamic integer and float getter loops fall from develop 612.372/626.254 to feature 166.515/166.789 ns/item, reductions of 72.808/73.367% for the entire branch. Plain Java is 0.897/0.915; boundary controls 3.296/3.777; read-lock controls 8.606/8.289 ns/item. All remain faster than Qore, despite the retained getter improvement. The controls differ in dispatch, locking, observable frames and lifetime semantics; none establishes an equivalent implementation or a hardware lower bound. Do not attribute the whole branch/develop improvement to the latest getter change alone.

CSV report, object orders, callback pipeline and text index use 12.756%, 11.207%, 72.109% and 21.419% less time than develop respectively. These four synthetic processing mixes show broader impact, not one universal application-performance score. List mutation improves 9.332% but remains 44.30x the Java workload time; it is still an important execution bottleneck.

Temporary hash is the sole aggregate or layout loss in this 55-workload checkpoint: 325.286 to 335.190 ns/item, +3.045%. All three layout medians are slower (+3.341%, +3.506%, +3.045%); default observed fork-mean ranges are disjoint, while reverse and shuffle ranges overlap. Preserve this regression for follow-up; the checkpoint does not attribute its cause or dismiss it as noise. Observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

Ten serial untimed profiles retain all raw samples. Feature getter traces enter the admitted helper and typed companion, with live member lookup/read locking, RuntimeConfig acquisition, observable frame work, receiver reloads and ownership cleanup still present. Feature polymorphic traces show native dispatch plus checked receiver/local-slot setup and reference bookkeeping. Capturing closures retain live capture lookup/read locking and native frame work. List mutation retains generic path navigation, compound assignment, local access and value cleanup. Waiting signal-thread samples are not hot-path CPU work; sample counts are not cycles or isolated call latency.

The new Java controls passed 72 result checks and 1200 independent cross-reference cases. Bytecode review confirms identical normalized loop structure across plain/boundary/locked forms and finally-protected read-lock release. Compiler logs confirm plain getter/callback inlining, preserved boundary hints, and all six loop bodies reaching level4 during the first diagnostic warmup. Those instrumented durations are excluded; this does not guarantee identical compilation histories in every subsequent JVM fork.

The next separate experiment is explicit RuntimeConfig threading through ordinary AOT dispatch, reusing a live same-thread view already acquired by generated callers where possible. Preserve legacy helper ABIs, full live dispatch keys, selected variants, debugger/body readiness, object validity, exception/ownership cleanup, cancellation and reader-safe stack publication; legacy fallback snapshot refresh remains. Measure register pressure, cold/miss paths and broad controls. TLS is one remaining cost, not a demonstrated explanation for the entire Java gap.

The only development failure was a premeasurement environment guard: nested macOS Python launching prepended MANPATH. No timed job ran. Exact-interpreter reuse preserved every environment key/value/order, the fingerprint guard was unchanged, and a fresh prepared matrix passed. The failed preflight, original driver hash and all subsequent successful results are retained. No measured sample was discarded or retried.

The full audit-changes checklist and independent raw-result replay must pass
before this evidence is committed. Subsequent RuntimeConfig threading is a
separate before/after experiment: reuse a live same-thread view, preserve live
Program/class/parse-option and fallback semantics, and measure broad controls.
No Java parity or justified global performance ceiling is established.


## Rejected explicit RuntimeConfig for ordinary AOT dispatch (post-bf4b4ebdd)

The candidate is rejected after conservative manual review despite passing the original mechanical rule. The getter targets improve, but monomorphic-call aggregate time increases 5.430%/5.251% in screen/confirmation and the side-effecting method loop increases 3.132%/8.782%. The original rule/result is unchanged and preserved separately; overlapping observed ranges do not establish non-regression. Production changes and the two new fixture files are restored/removed only after archival, followed by fresh Release/Debug qualification.

This is a matched before/after experiment against the merged branch at `bf4b4ebddfb8f778527d81ac3f514ddeb0e9d27a`, not a new develop/Java comparison. Both runtimes use Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG` and qcc `-O3`. The matrix contains 55 workloads (37 micro, 4 mixed, 14 getter/control), three fixed layouts, 4096 items/seed7, three warmup and three measured 300ms windows per job. ### Retention rule and adverse results

Both integer and floating getter-loop targets must use at least 2% less aggregate time and improve in every fixed layout in both epochs. Reject a non-target workload/layout that is at least 3% slower with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges in both epochs. Reverse and shuffle487 orders are fixed from the new baseline default symbols and shared exactly with the candidate; there is no alignment search, dropped window or rescue epoch.

Screen: 25 aggregate losses and 78 adverse workload/layout comparisons. Largest layout loss: `string_result_loop`, `reverse`, +6.743950%. Every loss and observed fork range is retained in the raw report.

Confirmation: 26 aggregate losses and 81 adverse workload/layout comparisons. Largest layout loss: `effect_loop`, `reverse`, +13.873874%. Every loss and observed fork range is retained in the raw report.

Repeated adverse comparisons meeting the original broad-regression rule: none.

Observed ranges are not confidence intervals; overlapping ranges do not establish non-regression. All adverse confirmation comparisons have overlapping ranges, some very wide; no outliers were removed. The manual rejection is a conservative engineering judgment, not a new statistical test or proof that the candidate alone caused each slowdown. Host frequency, thermals and unrelated load are uncontrolled. No task-owned builds, tests, profiles or source analysis overlapped timing.

### Implementation and qualification

The candidate threads a borrowed live native RuntimeConfig through versioned ordinary AOT helpers. Callers reuse an existing non-null fast view or acquire a separate nullable view once at logical entry; final lowering coalesces an earlier ordinary acquisition with a later-encountered callback acquisition only when same-block ordering proves dominance. Legacy exports remain. No Program/class/options snapshot is substituted for live state. Complete dispatch keys, private access, signature/body/readiness/debugger guards, live member locks, logical frames, argument ownership, fallback snapshot refresh and per-iteration cancellation remain.

Fresh baseline Release/Debug each pass 69 core files / 112 cases / 17,595 assertions; candidate each passes 70 / 115 / 17,825, including 230 new assertions. Fresh restored Release/Debug each pass the original 69 / 112 / 17,595 after candidate removal. Qualification also includes 13 lvalue/DGC suites, local HTTP/REST, 7 merged DataProvider suites, offline LLM, thread cancellation, 555 IR + 555 AOT reference checks and 1985 Debug native checks in each enabled/disabled mode. All 64 owned qmods are rebuilt and their Release aliases restored, with unrelated links unchanged. The filtered REST checks execute one selected case per module; QUnit summary totals include skipped cases. No external database suite was run. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer/cross-platform certification.

Actual legacy baseline executables are checked against the candidate runtime separately from timing. Optimized LLVM/assembly inspection verifies versioned dispatch selection and shared-view propagation; static code evidence is not a per-helper latency estimate or sole-cause proof. The fixture covers borrowed/object/consuming and throwing forms, fallbacks, traversal-order-independent acquisition reuse, and registration/teardown lifetimes.

Development records preserve the baseline REST output-format harness failure, unsupported numbered patch-hunk formatting before source application, a prematurely started qualification cancelled before application, and the new fixture's `bool(...)` parse error corrected to logical conversion. The corrected fixture passes 230 assertions; final Release/Debug qualification is fresh. An initial inspection summary incorrectly counted zero instructions because its address parser omitted Mach-O colons; that summary is invalid and archived. The corrected parser requires positive counts, and all 118 raw assembly/symbol outputs match between inspection attempts. No timed samples were discarded or retried.

See `results-aot-ordinary-dispatch-runtime-config-rejected-macos-arm64.json` for all raw windows, hashes, commands, logs, failed attempts, code/layout diagnostics, the independent replay and complete 62-item audit. No new Java ratio or global performance ceiling is established. The next separate hypothesis is moving immutable zero-argument signature/return-family proof into existing generic admission, without widening native eligibility or changing live guards, binding readiness, locks or frames.

### Prospective retention rule and adverse results

Both integer and floating getter-loop targets must use at least 2% less aggregate time and improve in every fixed layout in both epochs. Reject any non-target workload with at least 3% aggregate slowdown in both epochs, regardless of observed range overlap. Also reject a repeated same-workload/layout slowdown of at least 3% with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges. These rules were frozen before this experiment; they do not retroactively change the preceding RuntimeConfig experiment.

Reverse and shuffle487 orders are fixed from the baseline default symbols and shared exactly with the candidate. No alignment search, dropped window, pooling or rescue epoch is permitted.

Screen: 19 aggregate losses and 76 adverse workload/layout comparisons. Largest layout loss: `string_result_loop` / `shuffle-487`, +5.868094%. All losses and observed ranges are preserved in the raw report.

No confirmation epoch was run after the failed target screen, so repeatability of non-target regressions was not assessed. Rejection follows the failed target gate, not a claim that every observed loss is a repeatable regression.

Failed target checks:

- screen / `float_loop` / aggregate reduction at least 2%: -0.673476% time.
- screen / `float_loop` / default: +0.475157% time.

Observed ranges are not confidence intervals; overlap does not prove non-regression. Host frequency, thermals and unrelated load are uncontrolled. No task-owned builds, tests, profiles, edits or source analysis overlapped timing. Static instruction evidence does not establish sole timing causality.

### Implementation, footprint and qualification

The candidate runtime recorded a strongly typed byte-sized return-family proof before immutable full-key PIC publication. Exact zero-formal/supplied arity, canonical hard int/float return identity and absence of type substitution were proved at admission. The outlined getter reused only those facts. This was neither native body eligibility nor a cached binding: the compiler proof and matching positive typed companion remained independently required. Missing/default, optional/soft/enum and generic signatures retained ordinary behavior.

Original caller lowering and the eight-argument internal helper ABI remain unchanged. Live Program/object/private-access/epoch checks, debugger state, exact AOT body/readiness, ARGV and parameterized-receiver guards, member locks, eager object/class context, reader-safe logical frames, stack checks, ownership cleanup and cancellation remain. RuntimeConfig is still acquired through TLS after positive getter admission; no context deferral, cached member value or negative binding cache is introduced. Frame diagnostics still read signature metadata.

Compiled macOS arm64 probes measure cache-entry size 240 -> 240 bytes, alignment 8 -> 8, and actual allocator block 256 -> 256 bytes (malloc_good_size 256 -> 256). The new enum is at offset 233, after the existing scalar-parameter flag at offset 232; existing measured offsets remain unchanged. This targeted layout check is not an application-memory measurement.

The compiled getter helper grows from 582 to 608 total instructions and its native stack frame from 352 to 368 bytes. The cold admission helper grows from 741 to 760 instructions, with its 288-byte stack frame unchanged. The getter removes the substitution-query call and uses the admitted byte, but register allocation and other generated code change too. These static whole-function counts include cold and cleanup paths; they are not executed instruction counts or proof of timing causality. No general memory-cost reduction is claimed.

Actual exported runtime function names match. The two getter probe callers have identical LLVM bodies after removing only debug-metadata IDs; exact executable/helper assembly and all operands are retained for review. Actual baseline executables pass their micro/mixed/probe reference grids on the candidate runtime with loaded-library identity checked. These are untimed diagnostics, not additional performance samples.

All nine matched relocatable text sections have equal lengths, but only the three mixed-suite pairs are byte-identical; micro/probe pairs differ. Equal generated function/instruction counts are not executable identity. Relocations, placement and runtime code can influence timings. The initial supplemental byte parser stopped because objdump appended disassembly after the raw section; its original script/output are preserved, with the original terminal status unavailable after tool-output truncation. The corrected explicit-section parser completed successfully before timing, without changing any measured binary.

Qualified baseline Release/Debug each pass 69 core files / 112 cases / 17,595 assertions. Candidate Release/Debug each pass 69 / 112 / 17,659, including the expanded getter suite's 1,117 assertions (64 more QUnit assertions; additional native C++ assertions are not counted as QUnit assertions). Fresh restored Release/Debug each pass 69 / 112 / 17,595 after candidate removal. The expanded exclusion fixture also passes AST/IR on the unchanged frozen baseline. Tests verify positive cache proofs, excluded return signatures, independently type-correct companion slots, absent matching binding and delayed rebinding. Existing debugger, concurrent reader/writer, cross-Program, epoch, stack-limit and readiness coverage remains.

Qualification rebuilds all 64 owned qmods and restores their Release aliases with unrelated links unchanged. It includes 13 lvalue/DGC suites, local HTTP/REST, seven merged DataProvider suites, offline LLM, thread cancellation, 555 IR + 555 AOT reference checks and 1,985 Debug native checks in each enabled/disabled mode. Filtered REST summaries include skipped cases; only the single selected case per module is claimed. No external database suite was run. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer/cross-platform certification.

See `results-aot-getter-signature-admission-rejected-macos-arm64.json` for every measured window, exact sources/artifacts, commands, logs, any development attempts, independent replay and all 62 audit-changes checks. No new Java ratio or global performance ceiling is established.

The next independent investigation is compiler recognition of stable auto parameters selected by boxed PHIs feeding method receivers. Existing entry-owner, strong-slot identity and reflective-mutation epoch guards must remain; the direct receiver-only ownership set must not be widened. This addresses repeated receiver-local reloads visible in the historical optimized profile, not signature admission. It is a hypothesis, not an implemented or measured improvement, and does not revive the rejected all-auto-parameter heuristic.

### Predeclared decision and limits

Both getter-loop targets must use at least 5% less aggregate time than both before and compile-disabled, with every fixed layout faster, in both epochs. Reject a non-target workload with at least 3% aggregate slowdown against the same comparator in both epochs, regardless of observed range overlap; also reject a repeated same-workload/comparator/layout slowdown of at least 3% with disjoint observed ranges. No dropped window, epoch pooling, rescue trial or layout search is allowed.

Repeated aggregate adverse comparisons: `monomorphic_call` / `before`, `monomorphic_call` / `compile_disabled`. Repeated disjoint adverse layout comparisons: `indirect_call` / `before` / `default`, `monomorphic_call` / `before` / `default`, `monomorphic_float_call` / `compile_disabled` / `shuffle-487`.

Observed ranges are not confidence intervals; overlap does not prove non-regression. Host frequency, thermals and unrelated load are uncontrolled. No task-owned builds, tests, profiles, source reads, edits or analysis overlapped timing. No new Java ratio or global performance ceiling is established.

### Compiler proof, generated code and qualification

The rejected candidate used a separate iterative, cycle-safe compiler worklist following only boxed PHIs that feed method receivers. It extended the profitability heuristic for otherwise eligible read-only auto parameters; it does not prove an object type or method target. The direct receiver-only ownership set is unchanged. Missing definitions, native PHIs and other value-producing operations stop traversal; roots, vertices and edges check cancellation every 100 iterations. Expected hash-table complexity is linear in visited values and edges.

Existing entry ownership, actual strong-slot identity, private-entry exclusions and reflective mutation epochs remain required. References, weak values and non-objects keep ordinary reloads. A reflective write permanently defeats reuse for that invocation; newly installed references remain live on later reads. No runtime helper ABI, serialized IR, method dispatch, Program/access/binding guard, frame, member lock or cleanup contract changes. The candidate applied when producing AOT code and required recompilation; no IR/JIT timing benefit is claimed.

Actual probe LLVM shows three guarded receiver parameters in each candidate object, float and string probe, absent in baseline and compile-disabled. The disabled and baseline bodies match after removing only debug-metadata IDs. Ordinary reload fallback calls remain emitted. Exact executable/runtime assembly and every operand are archived; static counts include cold paths and are not executed instruction counts or timing causality. Exported runtime function names match, and actual baseline executables pass all three reference grids on the candidate runtime with loaded-library identity checked.

In the default layout, each selected object, float and string probe grows from 1534 to 1666 static instructions and from a 768-byte to an 848-byte stack frame. These whole-function counts include cold paths; they do not establish why unrelated fast-call workloads regressed.

All 27 executable/object byte sizes and single-build compile durations are recorded. These are diagnostics, not a statistically controlled compilation-throughput or application-memory comparison; no zero-cost footprint claim is made.

Fresh baseline Release/Debug each pass 69 core files / 112 cases / 17595 assertions; candidate each passes 69 / 112 / 18219. Restored Release/Debug each pass 69 / 112 / 17595. The expanded fixture is checked in AST and AOT at `-O0`/`-O3` on the unchanged baseline. The initial IR check failed reflective variable lookup in the existing `objectCacheOptional`; the unchanged fixture reproduces it, and reduced new cases also fail in `phiCacheReflect`. Disabling IR context elision does not repair it. Those failures are preserved; no full-fixture IR pass is claimed for this AOT-only change. Candidate checks cover nested conditional receivers, reflective backedges, mutable references, weak/non-object and pseudo receivers, written/captured/address-escaped parameters, scalar-only PHIs, one-read exclusions and the compile-disable control. Existing direct-receiver/private-entry checks remain.

Qualification rebuilds all 64 owned qmods and restores exactly their Release aliases with unrelated links unchanged. Each runtime also runs ten newly merged CSV/DataProvider/line-iterator suites in AST and IR, the existing DataProvider/local HTTP/REST/offline LLM/thread checks, 13 lvalue/DGC suites and 555 IR + 555 AOT references; Debug runs 1985 native checks in each enabled/disabled mode. Filtered REST summaries include skips; only the selected case per module is claimed. No external database suite was run. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer/cross-platform certification.

See `results-aot-phi-receiver-param-cache-rejected-macos-arm64.json` for all 11880 measured windows, commands, exact sources/artifacts, development attempts, independent replay and all 62 audit-changes checks. Further optimization and a fresh Java/develop checkpoint require independent validation; this experiment does not establish Java parity or a global ceiling.

Next independently test an exact `NOTHING` exit before the late scalar cleanup guard in existing AOT native-call continuations. Current monomorphic assembly still tests scalar tag families on empty cleanup values after merging native and generic paths. The proposed change must retain every nonempty cleanup operation at its original point; emitted-code inspection and fresh measurements are required before claiming a benefit. The baseline IR reflective-frame discrepancy remains a separate correctness follow-up.


## Rejected exact-empty AOT cleanup exit (post-d7e14c3af)

The candidate failed the predeclared screen and is rejected. Its compiler/test changes are archived and restored, with fresh selected Release/Debug qualification. This is an optimized branch before/after/control comparison, not a new Java/develop checkpoint.

Candidate base: `d7e14c3af2a12886a302b185c0add0cc8542ce43`, including merged origin/develop `7a79146311e041a4cd24ac6c8a8e652f60dc5f32`. The frozen baseline core was qualified at `815eeb76120d6cded9a1bea8caca78041149c85a`. The intervening reviewed changes are evidence/docs and DataProvider/DataFrame code, with no core/compiler/benchmark change; all 55 benchmark fixtures require no modules. Newly merged modules were separately rebuilt and tested. The older full-core qualification is not claimed to cover the newer module revision. The compile-disabled comparator uses the exact candidate compiler/runtime and additionally isolates the proposed lowering.

Both runtimes use Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`; all AOT executables use qcc `-O3`. Modes are before, candidate and candidate compiled with `QORE_DISABLE_AOT_EMPTY_CLEANUP_GUARD=1`, absent during execution. Layouts are default, reverse and shuffle-487; nondefault modes share exact baseline-derived order files, without layout search.

The fixed screen has 55 workloads, three layouts, three modes and three forks: 1485 processes / 4455 measured windows. Each process uses 4096 items / seed 7, three warmup and three measured 300 ms windows. Order seed: 137021. The conditional five-fork confirmation (seed 137023) was not run because the screen failed. No dropped samples, rescue run, threshold change or epoch pooling.

### Decision and limitations

Both integer and floating monomorphic-call targets must use at least 5% less aggregate time than both controls and improve in every fixed layout, in both screen and confirmation. Repeated non-target aggregate losses of at least 3% against the same control reject regardless of range overlap; repeated same-workload/control/layout losses of at least 3% with disjoint observed ranges also reject. A failed screen ends the experiment.

Integer monomorphic calls change +1.966691% versus before / +3.006283% versus disabled. Floating monomorphic calls change -4.013055% / -1.214391%. Neither satisfies the target gate; default-layout float calls are also +1.415884% slower versus before. Integer calls are slower in default and reverse, with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges, but faster in shuffle-487. A favorable layout alone does not establish a robust gain.

Other screen-only aggregate losses include indirect float calls (+5.176959% / +5.773762%), indirect integer-result calls (+8.361254% / +6.731426%) and the two-read getter loop (+6.688867% / +1.032202%). They are not labelled repeated confirmed regressions because no confirmation was run. The target failure alone requires rejection.

Observed ranges are not confidence intervals; overlap does not prove non-regression. Host thermals, frequency and unrelated load are uncontrolled. No task-owned builds, tests, profiles, source reads, edits or analysis overlapped timing. No new Java ratio, IR/JIT gain or global performance ceiling is established.

### Generated code and qualification

The rejected compiler change adds an exact `VAL_NOTHING` exit before late AOT scalar cleanup tag-family checks. Native continuations place zero in boxed cleanup slots; generated `cbz` branches can skip the remaining checks. Every nonempty value retains the original cleanup operation at the original program point. No ABI, serialized IR, TLS, RuntimeConfig, frame, lock, epoch or cancellation guard change; earlier publication guards are unchanged.

Actual post-optimization LLVM confirms zero-valued native PHI inputs and exact-empty guards. The four inspected monomorphic/indirect bodies match baseline when the candidate is compile-disabled, after removing only debug-metadata attachments. Decref call counts remain 27 / 28 / 17 / 30. Exact prepared executable assembly was inspected before timing. Default-layout instruction counts grow from 720 to 776 (integer monomorphic), 706 to 807 (float monomorphic), 467 to 504 (fast indirect) and 713 to 776 (ordinary indirect). These are whole-function static counts including cold paths, not executed instruction counts or proof of causality. All 27 object/executable sizes and single-build compile durations are retained as diagnostics, not compilation-throughput or application-memory measurements.

Exported runtime names match, and actual before executables pass all three reference grids against the candidate runtime with loaded-library identity verified. The initial before-preflight otool parser expected colon-delimited addresses and produced empty summaries. The original raw executable/disassembly is preserved, the parser was corrected before candidate/control inspection, and `corrected-selected-assembly.json` plus `inspection-erratum.json` supersede those empty summaries. No timing inference uses them.

Candidate Release and Debug each pass 71 core files / 114 cases / 18245 assertions, including control coverage in the existing native-assignment and value-tag fixtures. Fresh restored Release and Debug each pass 69 / 112 / 17595. Each also runs 13 lvalue/DGC suites (82 cases; 1330 Release / 2663 Debug assertions), three thread-cancellation suites, 20 upstream AST/IR checks, eight DataProvider suites, DataFrame regressions and 555 IR + 555 AOT reference checks. Debug runs 1985 native checks with the diagnostic control both unset and set; after restoration the removed control has no effect. All 64 owned qmods are rebuilt and their Release aliases restored with unrelated links unchanged. Independent raw-log/source/artifact replay checks both candidate and restoration. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer/cross-platform certification.

See `results-aot-empty-cleanup-rejected-macos-arm64.json` for every measured window, all gains/losses, exact source/artifact provenance, commands/logs, inspection correction, independent replay and the 62-item audit. No production optimization from this experiment is retained.

Next investigate finite literal-key selection in nonescaping temporary hashes. Existing fixed-hash scalar replacement handles a single constant key but rejects a key selected through a PHI. Any extension must prove every selected key exists, preserve duplicate-key and evaluation-order semantics, prove predecessor dominance and inline-value lifetime, and retain arbitrary/missing-key, mutable/reference/captured/reflective fallbacks. Actual IR feasibility and fresh validation/measurements remain required; this is a separate hypothesis, not a demonstrated speedup.

### Decision and limitations

The target must use at least 10% less aggregate time than both controls and improve in every fixed layout in both phases. Reject any non-target workload at least 3% slower in aggregate than the same control in both phases, regardless of range overlap. Also reject repeated same-workload/control/layout losses of at least 3% with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges. A failed screen ends the experiment; this screen passed, so the predeclared confirmation was run.

Temporary hashes: 339.732199 -> 40.988696 ns/item in the screen (-87.934998% versus before / -87.750197% versus disabled), and 338.724517 -> 40.685528 in confirmation (-87.988608% / -87.915902%). Every target layout improves. This is a reproducible benefit for the rejected prototype, not a retained branch improvement.

No non-target aggregate loss reaches 3% in both phases. The `default_loop` screen loss of +4.882727% versus before falls to +1.178898% in confirmation. Nevertheless, `indirect_affine` / `compile_disabled` / `reverse` loses +6.140863% in the screen and +10.222115% in confirmation. Comparator fork-mean ranges are 6.816923..6.893671 and 6.751688..7.033329 ns/item; candidate ranges are 7.141789..7.623612 and 7.175289..7.858892. Those disjoint repeated losses independently require rejection.

The three-layout `indirect_affine` aggregate is +0.236603% versus disabled in the screen and -0.006699% in confirmation; this does not override the layout gate. Other confirmation-only disjoint losses include reverse-layout indirect-float-result and wide affine-indirect calls. All layouts and both controls remain in the evidence; no claim of general non-regression is made.

Observed fork-mean ranges are not confidence intervals, and overlap does not establish non-regression. Host load, frequency and thermals are uncontrolled. No task-owned build, test, profile, source read, edit or analysis job overlapped either timed phase. No fresh Java/develop ratio, IR/JIT timing benefit, Java parity or global performance ceiling is established.

### Generated code and qualification

The rejected shared IR analysis projects an immutable private exact-integer hash read through a two-to-four-edge literal-string PHI into a native integer PHI. It proves actual predecessor identity, no backedge, initializer/read/edge dominance and inline-integer lifetime bounds; a native integer tag alone is not a lifetime proof. Existing duplicate-key-last-value behavior and private-local visibility/noescape restrictions remain. Arbitrary or missing keys, wide values, unsupported joins, mutations, references, captures, embedded-NUL keys and exceptional-flow functions retain existing paths. Selector strings and their ownership deliberately remain.

The audit moved whole-key-set validation outside the per-read resolver, avoiding repeated scans, and conservatively excluded exceptional-flow functions because this pass receives a normal-flow CFG. The existing instruction scan checks both base exception targets and Throw/Rethrow targets. Unbounded new analysis checks cancellation; bounded selector/predecessor walks retain their explicit limits. No runtime helper ABI, TLS, RuntimeConfig, frame, lock, epoch or cancellation-poll contract changes.

Actual prepared ordinary/fast temporary-hash bodies shrink from 436/432 to 169/159 static instructions. LLVM and assembly show the hash allocation, dynamic lookup and two runtime local reloads removed; two static branch-local string allocation sites (one selected per iteration), refself and decrefs remain. Stack/cancellation checks and body-local setup/teardown remain. These whole-function counts include cold paths and are not executed instruction counts or latency estimates.

Compile-disabled target LLVM matches before after removing only debug attachments. Across all 150 microbenchmark LLVM definitions, removing debug attachments and substituting exact private/internal string declarations for renumbered references leaves only the two target bodies and startup `main` different; startup metadata differs separately. The normalization and raw code are preserved. This comparison does not prove the cause of the unrelated timing regression. Runtime helper API names match; runtime text names show six compiler-lambda renames and three additional compiler/STL implementations, not new runtime helper APIs. Actual before executables pass all three reference grids on the candidate runtime with loaded-library identity verified.

All 27 object/executable byte sizes and single-build compile durations are retained as diagnostics. They are not statistically controlled compilation-throughput or application-memory measurements.

The new semantic fixture passes on the qualified baseline in AST, IR, JIT, tiered and AOT modes. Candidate focused validation includes 254 finite-key assertions, with positive allocation removal and negative allocation retention; exact integer extremes, duplicate/empty/unicode keys, loop grids, observable keys, aliases, references, captures and thrown/nonthrown catch-rejoin paths are covered. Enabled/disabled IR/JIT/tiered and AOT `-O0`/`-O3`, stripped source, EH, no-debug-info and split-compilation variants are included.

Candidate Release and Debug each pass 72 core files / 115 cases / 18401 assertions. Freshly restored Release and Debug each pass 69 / 112 / 17595. Each also runs 13 lvalue/DGC suites (82 cases; 1330 Release / 2663 Debug assertions), three thread-cancellation suites, 20 upstream AST/IR checks, eight DataProvider suites, DataFrame regressions and 555 IR + 555 AOT references. Debug runs 1985 native checks with the diagnostic control both unset and set; after restoration the removed control has no effect. All 64 owned qmods are rebuilt and their exact Release aliases restored, with unrelated links unchanged. Independent raw-log/source/artifact replay covers candidate and restored builds. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-suite/sanitizer/cross-platform certification.

Initial attempts are preserved separately with actual nonzero terminal statuses: a wrong generated-header path during freezing, a one-entry-versus-two-entry disassembly collector assumption, an intentional duplicate-key warning rejected by a strict collector, an explicit C++ value-constructor compilation error, an interrupted launch before that correction, and a collector expecting a QUnit summary from a silent-success fixture. Two broad runs were intentionally stopped before Debug for the premeasurement audit corrections. Final focus, code inspection and complete qualification were repeated on the corrected source before timing. None of those failed/interrupted attempts is relabelled as successful qualification.

See `results-aot-finite-hash-key-rejected-macos-arm64.json` for all 11880 windows, every gain/loss, commands and raw logs, exact source/artifact provenance, independent replay, archived/restored sources and the full 62-item audit. No compiler/test implementation from this experiment is retained.

Next independently investigate elimination of the exclusive literal-selector graph after successful hash projection. The remaining string allocation/refself/decrefs are visible in actual generated code. Start with direct literal PHIs and private exact-string single-store locals whose every consumer is eliminated; retain observable strings, linked/shared/partially projected graphs, exceptional flows and all ownership/cancellation contracts. This is a materially different hypothesis requiring fresh validation and predeclared broad measurements, not an unchanged retry or a demonstrated benefit. A fresh optimized Java/develop checkpoint follows a meaningful retained improvement; the separate baseline IR reflective-frame discrepancy remains a correctness follow-up.

## Rejected finite hash selector elision (post-c80d44b03)

This experiment is **rejected; its compiler and fixture changes are not retained**. It combines finite literal-key integer-hash projection with a complete-use proof that removes private selector strings and their PHI/local storage. Observable, copied, linked, referenced, captured, exceptional, or partially projected cases keep their required operations. No runtime helper ABI, TLS, frame, lock, epoch, or cancellation-poll convention changes. This is distinct from the rejected projection-only predecessor recorded at `0a30967c2`.

The baseline is the resolved `origin/develop` merge committed as `c80d44b03` (develop `f6c33ac63`). It was built and qualified before the merge commit, with `0a30967c2` as Git HEAD and the resolved merge tree in the working directory; every tracked source byte was verified identical after the merge commit. The report distinguishes build-time HEAD from source commit.

All timings use Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG` and `qcc -O3`: 55 workloads, three predetermined link layouts, and four modes. `Before` is the frozen qualified baseline; `Candidate` enables both transformations; `Pass off` disables the entire finite-key projection in the candidate compiler; `Selector off` retains projection but disables selector removal. Both controls use the candidate runtime, and both disabling flags are absent during execution. A three-fork screen is followed by a five-fork confirmation only if the target passes. Each fork uses 4096 items with seed 7 and three warmup plus three measured 300 ms windows. No owned build, test, profile, edit, or analysis overlaps timing.

Values below are ns/item: the median of three layout medians of fork means. Negative changes mean less time. Every sample, workload, layout, gain and loss is retained; epochs are not pooled. Observed ranges are not confidence intervals. These are whole-workload timings, not isolated call latency or a production-throughput score, and they provide no new Java/develop or IR/JIT comparison or global performance ceiling.

### Decision and validation

The target must improve at least 10% in aggregate and improve every layout against all three controls, in both epochs. A repeated non-target aggregate loss of at least 3%, or a repeated same-workload/control/layout loss of at least 3% with disjoint observed fork-mean ranges, rejects the candidate.

Failed target checks: 0. Repeated aggregate adverse results: 1. Repeated disjoint-layout adverse results: 3.

- Repeated aggregate loss: `monomorphic_call` versus `compile_disabled`.

- Repeated disjoint loss: `indirect_float` versus `before` in `shuffle-487`.

- Repeated disjoint loss: `indirect_float` versus `compile_disabled` in `shuffle-487`.

- Repeated disjoint loss: `monomorphic_float_call` versus `projection_only` in `reverse`.

Selected Release/Debug qualification passed (baseline: 70 core fixtures/117 cases/17609 assertions per runtime; candidate: 73 core fixtures/120 cases/18673 assertions per runtime). Each runtime additionally passed 48 upstream AST/IR runs, integration and cancellation suites, 13 lvalue/DGC fixtures, 555 IR plus 555 AOT reference checks; Debug passed 1985 native tests in each control. 79 qmods were rebuilt and their Release aliases restored. Debug ML uses a documented path-only adaptation. This is not full-suite, sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

The prototype sources were archived recoverably and removed/restored; the restored baseline was freshly qualified and independently verified before publication. Experimental gains are not branch gains.

Next, investigate a distinct AOT-only redundant exception-sink check proof. The current generated direct-call loop rechecks the sink after both the slow cancellation helper and the fast polling path. A candidate must prove the sink clear on every incoming fast path, invalidate that proof across any potentially modifying operation, and preserve all live cancellation loads, slow helper calls, thread-exit checks, exception cleanup and entry checks. Inspect actual generated code and negative cases before committing to measurements; no installed implementation or measured benefit is established yet. Do not retry the rejected selector version unchanged.

Full raw samples, controls, source identities, generated-code inspection and qualification evidence: [results-aot-finite-key-selector-rejected-macos-arm64.json](results-aot-finite-key-selector-rejected-macos-arm64.json).

## Rejected proved-clear AOT exception-sink checks (post-02ce653ed)

Rejected: direct calls take 1.552219 ns/item before and 1.555521 with the candidate
(+0.212729%); the compile-disabled control takes 1.544499 (+0.713660% versus that
control). The predeclared target required at least 5% less aggregate time against
both controls and an improvement in every fixed layout. It fails six of eight
target checks. No confirmation or rescue run was made. No runtime/compiler/test
change from this experiment is retained.

The late AOT pass used a compiler-owned sink-argument attribute and a bounded
must-clear CFG proof to bypass exact, complete exception-sink checks on clean
incoming edges. Entry, unknown calls, stores, partial checks and exceptional
paths remained conservative. Per-iteration cancellation polling, deferral order,
thread/program atomic loads, slow helper, null-context fallback and cleanup
were unchanged. No runtime helper ABI, TLS, frame, lock or Program convention
changed; IR/JIT lowering was unchanged.

Untimed inspection selected ten micro functions (20 bypassed edges). The actual
arm64 direct-call fast loop traverses 12 instructions instead of 18 on its clean
non-pending path, but the complete function remains 128 instructions. This
static reduction did not produce a throughput gain; it does not establish the
cause or a performance ceiling. Method-call LLVM was unchanged because a
potentially fallible receiver-reload path prevented the proof. Accordingly,
method calls were removed from the target set before any timing, with the
previous plan archived; they remain among all 55 regression workloads. The
5% target and repeated 3% regression rules were not changed.

order seed 137053. All 1485 runs / 4455 measured windows are retained. Pass off
uses the candidate compiler with QORE_DISABLE_AOT_CLEAR_SINK_CHECKS present only
while compiling; that control is absent at execution. The baseline is source
commit 02ce653ed, qualified at c80d44b03; only the three intervening audited
evidence/documentation files differ. Develop f6c33ac63 is already merged.

Values are the median of three layout medians of fork means, in ns/item;
negative changes mean less time. Observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

the report. No owned build/test/profile/edit/analysis overlaps timing. These are
whole-workload measurements, not isolated call latency or a fresh Java/develop
comparison, and they are not a single overall Qore performance score.

The candidate passed selected Release and Debug qualification: 79 core fixtures,
128 cases and 23395 assertions each. After recoverable archival and removal of
all 18 changed source/fixture files (15 restored, three new fixtures removed),
fresh restored Release and Debug qualification each passed 70 core fixtures,
117 cases and 17609 assertions. Each runtime also passed 48 upstream AST/IR
runs, eight DataProvider suites, DataFrame, three cancellation suites, 13 lvalue
fixtures (82 cases, 1330 Release / 2663 Debug assertions), and 555 IR plus 555
AOT reference checks. Debug passed 1985 native tests with the compile control
unset and set. All 79 owned qmods were rebuilt and their Release aliases
restored; unrelated aliases were preserved. This is selected macOS arm64
coverage, not full-suite, sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

Pre-timing fixture corrections and failed attempts are recorded: the initial
implicit destructor-reassignment fixture failed on baseline IR and was replaced
with explicit deletion; no-debug lowering contains location-update calls and
is correctly ineligible; 12 existing LLVM text matchers were updated to accept
only the exact optional sink annotation. Broad qualification was restarted and
passed. Those test changes are not retained either.

The original preparation command's final tool receipt was unavailable after
context recovery. Its recorded prepare-terminal exit code belongs to a newly
observed independent recovery preflight, not an inferred original process exit.
All 27 prepared binaries, source/artifact hashes, reference checks and loaded
library paths were reverified before timing. Actual timing/verification/decision
process exits were observed. Independent replay checks every raw timing window,
fixed order, summary, comparison, reference and artifact. Timed checksums are
parsed for observability, not independently recalculated per window; semantic
correctness is checked separately against the reference grids.

Next investigate indexed-list compound mutation, not an unchanged retry of this
pass. Existing code still resolves the root, navigates references/COW/type and
index rules, dispatches generic compound operations and reloads local state.
Explore a narrowly guarded integer update using current runtime metadata and
slot identity, retaining the full fallback for sharing, references, closures,
negative/sparse indices, weak values and reflection. Inspect actual selection
and measure a separately declared candidate; no implementation or gain is
established here. A fresh optimized Java/develop checkpoint follows a meaningful
retained improvement. The global performance ceiling remains unestablished.

## Rejected indexed integer update and two-member getter (post-cee5710b3)

Both candidates are **rejected and not retained**. Each reduced its target
workload substantially, but violated its predeclared repeated-layout
non-regression gate. The source was recoverably archived and restored; these
are experimental gains, not improvements now present on the branch.

The measured branch revision is `cee5710b3`, with develop `bca388c1b` merged.
A later fetch found develop `3f0019a6a` (185 additional commits, including
runtime/compiler changes). Those changes are not in these measurements.
Merge and qualify that revision before establishing the next candidate's
optimized baseline; do not reuse these timings as a post-merge comparison.

Each experiment used Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG` / qcc `-O3`, the exact frozen
qualified before runtime, the candidate, and the candidate with its compiler
selector disabled. There were 55 workloads and three fixed layouts (default,
reverse, shuffle487). Each screen used three forks; each disjoint confirmation
used five, with three 300 ms warmup and three 300 ms measured windows per fork.
All 4455 screen and 7425 confirmation windows per experiment are retained:
23760 measured windows in total, with no outlier removal or pooling of epochs.
No owned build/test/profile/edit/analysis overlapped timing.

### Implementation and validation

The indexed-update prototype selected a versioned, guarded integer-add helper
for a narrowly proved list lvalue path, preserving the generic fallback.
Generated target code replaced the compound helper while retaining cleanup
and cancellation. The getter prototype widened only pure zero-argument scalar
getter eligibility from one read to two, retaining a live checked/locked read
at each original position. It did not widen effectful/unary methods. A miss
replayed the ordinary body before any effect or owned heap result.

Every qualification also passed 56 upstream AST/IR checks, eight DataProvider
suites, DataFrame, three cancellation suites, indexed-compound checks in all
execution modes, 14 lvalue fixtures (84 cases; 1391 Release / 2724 Debug
assertions), and 555 IR plus 555 AOT reference checks. Debug native tests passed
in both normal and prepared-local-reload-disabled modes: 2016 assertions per
mode for indexed add and 1985 for the getter and restored source. All 79 owned
qmods were rebuilt and their exact Release aliases restored; unrelated aliases
were preserved. This is selected macOS arm64 coverage, not full-repository,
sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

Failure and recovery records are preserved. The initial indexed test assumed
negative indices were invalid, contrary to baseline behavior. A weak-root
AST/compiled discrepancy was separately reproduced on baseline and is not
fixed here; the final regression fixture instead exercises strong-owner
mutation with a weak observer. An early native-test driver required qmod-alias
recovery. The original indexed-source restore command failed on patch-hunk
syntax after archival; a separate recorded recovery restored HEAD. Five
tracked candidate files were independently reconstructed from HEAD and that
patch and matched to qualified/timed hashes; all other candidate source copies
and all restored bytes were checked. No failed receipt was replaced by a
successful one.

Independent replay checks all 23760 raw measured windows, randomized orders,
fork/layout/aggregate summaries and both rejection decisions. Raw qualification
logs, source/artifact lineage, references, compiler controls and loaded runtime
paths are checked separately. Timed checksums establish observability and are
not independently recomputed per window. Historical candidate Debug artifacts
may have been overwritten by restored builds; their original independent
verification and raw logs identify them, rather than current Debug bytes.
Runtime binaries remain local and are not embedded in the report.

After the evidence commit and upstream merge/qualification, investigate
captured-closure binding and generated code, then profile serially to choose
a distinct optimization. The current native capture helper
performs a capture-map lookup followed by a live synchronized integer read.
Avoiding lookup work must not cache values, weaken synchronization, retain a
closure beyond its observable lifetime, or trust an address after reuse.
No implementation or measured benefit for that hypothesis is established.
Do not retry either rejected candidate unchanged. Refresh matched optimized
Java/develop numbers after a meaningful retained improvement; two-member
getters need their own analogous Java controls. Java parity and a global
performance ceiling remain unestablished.

## Known-closure AOT dispatch (post-27cca0da3, 2026-10-21)

Merge `27cca0da3` incorporates develop `26f5581d5`. This checkpoint compares
the qualified merged branch with an additive known-closure callback route,
using optimized `-O3 -DNDEBUG` runtimes and `qcc -O3` executables. The frozen
baseline runtime was built before the merge commit from its identical source
tree; the candidate is bound by exact source and artifact hashes. These are
branch-before/candidate measurements, not a fresh develop or Java comparison.

The retained implementation adds `qore_rt_try_funcref_int_int_v5` with the
same invocation-owned descriptor and scratch ABI as v4. A closure cache miss
checks the live tag once and reaches the unchanged native closure admission
directly, avoiding the generic v3 frame and duplicate decoding. A proven
nonclosure uses the shared prepared-call implementation without redundant
closure probes. Old v3/v4 entries and the positive reusable function-reference
path remain. No closure or captured value is retained, no capture lock is
removed, and all live Program/body/readiness/signature/debugger/stack/exception
checks and lexical-context restoration remain.

Only eligible reusable `int(int)` AOT callback sites select v5. Other
signatures, non-reusable sites, IR interpretation and JIT lowering are unchanged.
`QORE_DISABLE_AOT_KNOWN_CLOSURE_ROUTE=1` at compilation selects v4 on the same
candidate runtime; it is absent during measurement. Existing runtime controls
for the closure miss route and dynamic closure entry keep their behavior.
Older AOT artifacts retain their original helper until recompiled.

### Getter and fallback probes

|!Workload|!Develop AOT ns/item|!Feature AOT ns/item|!Time change
|object_loop|622.307|169.648|-72.739%

|two_read_loop|736.302|381.266|-48.219%

|string_result_loop|697.669|415.263|-40.478%
|string_result_short|1625.559|1381.692|-15.002%

Getter loops rotate three receivers per operation, read twice with a callback
between reads, and accumulate results. Qore uses auto receivers and one
name-based call_function entry per 4096-item operation; Java uses statically
typed final classes and direct entry. No setup/dispatch cost is subtracted.
Plain Java is unrestricted. Boundary controls prevent getter/callback inlining;
read-lock controls also use nonfair ReentrantReadWriteLock. This is not Qore's
member locking, dynamic lookup/deletion, context, ownership or cancellation.

|!Workload|!Java control|!Java ns/item|!Feature / Java time|!Java allocated bytes/item
|object_loop|plain|0.917|184.960x|0.000021
|object_loop|boundary|3.290|51.569x|0.017653
|object_loop|read-lock|8.452|20.072x|0.105661
|float_loop|plain|0.949|183.584x|0.000021
|float_loop|boundary|3.690|47.230x|0.017663
|float_loop|read-lock|8.547|20.389x|0.105664

No Java equivalent is claimed for the remaining twelve getter/fallback probes
or for the four mixed workloads. Allocation is observed JVM allocation, not
retained memory. Instrumented compiler diagnostics are excluded from timings.

All smaller losses are retained too. Overlapping fork ranges do not prove

branch impact, not a new individual optimization's causal speedup.

### Validation and next optimization

Fresh executable checks pass 4698 AOT and 1566 IR references, plus 555 Java
micro and 72 Java getter references. Reference-harness tests pass 17 + 8 cases
and 12600 independent probe simulations. All actual libraries, source/artifact
hashes, fixed symbol orders and normalized optimized settings are verified.
The separate Java diagnostics pass 72 references and 1200 cross-formula checks;
plain getters/callback inline, controlled boundaries do not, and lock bytecode
releases on normal and exceptional paths. Their durations are not measurements.

No runtime source changed in this checkpoint. The previous commit's selected
Release/Debug qualification (70 core fixtures, 109 executed passes plus eight
platform skips, 18021 assertions per runtime) is reused by exact source and
artifact identity, not represented as newly executed. Full qualification logs,
skip ledgers, lvalue/GC/thread/context/SQL/native checks and restored module
aliases remain in the hash-bound parent report. This is not full-suite,
sanitizer or cross-platform certification.

Ordinary indirect calls predominantly execute the prepared reusable helper, generated loop/callee, and stack-location restoration. TLS lookup is a small residual in this sampled shape; replacing more TLS alone is unlikely to close this gap. The live call guards and stack-walker synchronization must remain correct.

Polymorphic calls spend substantial sampled work on pinned class-local assignment/cleanup, object reference accounting, class acceptance and guarded native dispatch, beyond the small scalar method bodies. Captured closures still show native admission, synchronized capture reads and deferred frame/stack checks.

List mutation still reaches generic lvalue navigation/compound arithmetic, local publication and boxed value retain/discard/type handling. The workload also includes list construction and subsequent reads; the whole Java ratio is not an indexed-add-only cost. The previously rejected indexed-add prototype must not be reinstated unchanged.

Temporary hashes show allocation/free, value cleanup, typed hash assignment and input checking in both runtimes. Sampling does not explain the measured 3.791% branch/develop loss causally. Hash optimization and layout attribution require a separate controlled experiment.

Integer and floating getter loops retain ordinary name-based dispatch, local reload/reference handling and checked member access around the admitted native getter. Their large gap to plain Java includes these semantics and the documented setup/dispatch differences, not just the getter body.

Next use these profiles and generated code to select a distinct call or
collection optimization, with predeclared before/after/control gates and broad
regression checks. Neither Java parity nor a justified performance ceiling has
been established. All 62 audit-changes items and strict table checks are recorded
before committing this evidence.

## Rejected AOT lvalue-loop cleanup guards (2026-10-21)

A late, loop-only immediate-value cleanup guard was tested against the frozen
branch baseline and the same candidate with its compiler selector disabled.
Only the list-mutation function changed in the prepared micro/getter LLVM.
Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, `qcc -O3`, three fixed layouts, three forks, three
warmups and three 300-ms samples: all 297 runs / 891 timed windows retained.

|!List mutation layout|!Before ns/item|!Candidate ns/item|!Selector off ns/item|!Time change vs before
|default|195.059994|186.213632|196.693410|-4.535%
|reverse|195.580925|187.075182|195.089963|-4.349%
|shuffle487|197.846591|188.798258|196.758005|-4.573%

Geometric layout means: **196.159 -> 187.359 ns/item**, or **4.486% less time**
(4.496% versus selector off). This misses the predeclared 5% threshold: the
candidate is rejected, with no confirmation retry or relaxed gate. The single
polymorphic/reverse/selector-off +3.083% disjoint screen comparison is retained,
but is not repeated regression evidence and is not the rejection reason.

All 6507 executable references passed. Focused candidate Release qualification
passed 15 total fixtures: 21 QUnit cases / 6054 assertions and two exit-status
fixtures, without skips. An initial outer harness incorrectly required QUnit
output from a silent fixture; its child passed, but the outer failure is
preserved and the entire focused gate was rerun. Machine code retains all
cleanup fallback sites and cancellation polls; the target grows from 782 to
831 static arm64 instructions with an unchanged 320-byte frame. A disassembler
import-label mismatch is documented and corrected with resolved `otool` output.

The prototype and two fixtures were archived recoverably and removed. Fresh
restored Release qualification passes 14 total fixtures: 20 QUnit cases / 5974
assertions and two exit-status fixtures; this is focused qualification, not
a full selected Release/Debug rerun. No performance improvement is retained.
Next investigate unconditional prepared-root refresh after compound mutation:
omit repeated local lookup and combine publication/cleanup, while retaining
live reference evaluation, COW, exception handling and owner rotation. This
is a separate, not-yet-measured hypothesis, not a retry of this guard policy.

These are whole-workload times, not new Java/develop ratios or isolated call
latencies; neither parity nor a global performance ceiling is established.

## Rejected AOT first-public-base acceptance (2026-10-21)

The merged feature baseline is `99e3268cb`, including develop `e8add51ad`.
The candidate added a versioned pinned receiver initializer. It retained live
raw/parameterized-object rules, slot checks, access-order fallback and real
reference ownership, but recognized exact self or first-public-base identity
without generic class lookup. No class/object/access decision was cached.

Optimized Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, `qcc -O3`, three fixed layouts, three warmups
and three 300-ms samples per fork. Screens use three forks and confirmations
five. Geometric layout means for the integer polymorphic-call workload:

|!Phase|!Before ns/item|!Candidate ns/item|!Selector off ns/item|!Time reduction vs before|!Time reduction vs selector off
|Targeted screen|22.620253|20.129421|22.002232|11.012%|8.512%

|Broad 55-workload confirmation|22.789126|20.043574|22.775862|12.048%|11.996%

All four target gates exceed the predeclared 5% minimum versus both controls,
with every target layout improving. Broad confirmation also reduces floating
polymorphic-call time from 22.816 to 20.909 ns/item (8.359% versus before;
9.652% versus disabled). These are whole-workload measurements, not isolated
call latency or a fresh Java/develop comparison.

The candidate is nevertheless rejected by the unchanged regression gate.
List-building geometric time is 3.203% slower than before in broad screen and
3.010% slower in confirmation, meeting the repeated >=3% aggregate rule.
Confirmation before/candidate/disabled: 27.035937/27.849839/27.818850 ns/item.
The disabled control shows essentially the same slowdown, pointing to a runtime
compilation/layout side effect rather than execution of the new acceptance path;
this is an inference, not a completed diagnosis. No unchanged retry, relaxed
threshold or runtime optimization is retained.

All 4896 runs / 14688 timed windows and every adverse result are preserved.
The targeted effect-loop/reverse slowdown did not repeat. Broad screen also
flags object_short/shuffle487 versus disabled and two_read_short/shuffle487
versus before; neither repeats. Broad confirmation has no disjoint-layout signal,
but the aggregate list-building rejection applies regardless of range overlap.

Only integer/float polymorphic receiver initializers change in benchmark LLVM:
v3-to-v4 helper substitutions. Disabled LLVM matches before after verifying
startup metadata length. The integer target retains 1228 ARM64 instructions,
a 496-byte frame, 48 static decref sites and unchanged cancellation/preparation.
The compiler also changes inlining inside unchanged-source v3 in the rebuilt
runtime, which is why the same-runtime disabled control is retained. Both
runtime helper disassemblies and the untimed profile are archived. Reference
checks: 6507 targeted, 7047 broad. Probe/mixed LLVM bodies are unchanged.

Candidate focused Release passes eight fixtures / eight cases / 9816 assertions,
with no skips; direct Debug units pass 2119 in both settings. The first native
test attempt failed nine expectations because fresh same-name class definitions
had unset structural hashes and were not equivalent. Both old/new acceptance
paths agreed. Initializing test-local empty-class hashes corrected the fixture;
a fresh full focused rerun passed. That failed attempt is preserved, not omitted.

The six production edits and existing-test change were archived and restored.
Fresh restored qualification passes eight Release fixtures / eight cases /
9634 assertions, plus 2024 Debug native assertions per setting. Indexed compound
and 61 weak-reference assertions pass; all 125 owned Release qmod aliases are
restored. These are focused gates, not full selected retention qualification.

Next diagnose frozen list-building code/profile differences and investigate
translation-unit isolation of the acceptance helper as a distinct implementation,
